BoundaryFormer (BF) uses slot attention for joint boundary prediction, with a separate trajectory decoder using boundary slot features. BF++ introduces Camera and Camera+LiDAR variants with metric ground-plane encoding, typed boundary/trajectory queries, long-range point anchors, image-space curve refinement, and conservative gated LiDAR fusion.
AI.result: On 211 evaluation routes, BF++-Camera achieved 63.0 Driving Score and BF++-Camera+LiDAR achieved 64.4, compared to 59.3 for SimLingo and 26.1 for TransFuser++. BF++ is 40x smaller than SimLingo and 10x smaller than TF++, while achieving higher scores.
AI.conclusion: Jointly predicting lane boundaries, work zone boundaries, and driving trajectories is a promising direction for safer AV operation in work zones. The dataset and model provide a strong foundation for future work in this critical safety domain.

title: Robust Workflow Generation via Adversarial Learning for Audio Deepfake Detection
summary: The rapid advancement of speech synthesis and voice conversion technologies has made audio deepfakes increasingly realistic, posing serious security risks in practical applications. While existing detection methods achieve strong performance under controlled conditions, they often fail to generalize under real-world perturbations and corruptions. In this paper, we propose ROGUE, a framework that dynamically constructs robust detection workflows by orchestrating multiple detection tools. ROGUE formulates workflow generation as a sequential decision-making problem and introduces a dual-agent paradigm, where a perturbation agent generates audio perturbations and a policy agent learns to select and execute detection tools under perturbed conditions. Through adversarial learning, ROGUE enables perturbation-aware tool selection, adaptive execution strategies, and improved robustness to distribution shifts. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and real-world corruptions demonstrate that ROGUE consistently outperforms strong baselines in both robustness and generalization. Our results highlight the effectiveness of adversarially optimized workflow generation for building reliable audio deepfake detection systems in real-world deployment settings.

AI.tldr: ROGUE is a framework that dynamically constructs robust audio deepfake detection workflows by orchestrating multiple detection tools through a dual-agent paradigm, enabling perturbation-aware tool selection and improved robustness to distribution shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing audio deepfake detection methods achieve strong performance under controlled conditions but fail to generalize under real-world perturbations and corruptions, posing serious security risks in practical applications.
AI.method: ROGUE formulates workflow generation as a sequential decision-making problem and introduces a dual-agent paradigm: a perturbation agent generates audio perturbations, and a policy agent learns to select and execute detection tools under perturbed conditions. Through adversarial learning, the framework enables perturbation-aware tool selection and adaptive execution strategies.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and real-world corruptions demonstrate that ROGUE consistently outperforms strong baselines in both robustness and generalization.
AI.conclusion: Adversarially optimized workflow generation is effective for building reliable audio deepfake detection systems in real-world deployment settings.

title: Position: It is Time to Virtualize Foundation Models with a Self-evolving Operating System Layer
summary: AI applications have shifted from single, monolithic foundation models (FM) to compound agentic systems. Yet today's stacks remain fragmented: even as protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) ease tool/agent connectivity, each framework embeds an implicit runtime for state, memory, budgets, and guardrails, making behavior non-portable and governance brittle. It mirrors computing before operating systems, when every program re-implemented basic services. This position paper argues that the field now needs a Foundation Model Operating System (FMOS) -- a system layer that virtualizes FM interactions analogous to how virtual machines abstract physical hardware, giving applications the illusion of dedicated, trustworthy FM instances with effectively unbounded capabilities. Internally, the FMOS orchestrates knowledge across memory tiers, model selection and resource allocation, and verification and policy enforcement. Like the human brain switching between fast intuition and slow deliberation, the FMOS learns when to intervene and when to let inference proceed directly and continuously adapting its policies based on operational experience.

AI.tldr: This position paper proposes a Foundation Model Operating System (FMOS) - a new system layer that virtualizes FM interactions analogous to virtual machines abstracting hardware. The FMOS would provide applications with dedicated, trustworthy FM instances with effectively unbounded capabilities by orchestrating knowledge across memory tiers, model selection, resource allocation, and policy enforcement.
AI.motivation: Current AI stacks are fragmented: even with protocols like MCP and A2A facilitating tool/agent connectivity, each framework embeds implicit runtimes for state, memory, budgets, and guardrails. This makes behavior non-portable and governance brittle, mirroring computing before operating systems when every program re-implemented basic services.
AI.method: This is a conceptual position paper presenting the FMOS architecture. The proposed FMOS would learn when to intervene (like slow deliberation) and when to let inference proceed directly (like fast intuition), continuously adapting policies based on operational experience.
AI.result: The paper presents the FMOS concept as a system layer that virtualizes FM interactions, providing applications with the illusion of dedicated FM instances while internally orchestrating knowledge across memory tiers, model selection, resource allocation, and verification/policy enforcement.
AI.conclusion: The field needs an FMOS to provide the abstraction layer that AI systems currently lack, enabling portable behavior and robust governance - analogous to how traditional operating systems abstracted hardware resources.

title: Randomized SVD Approximations for Spectral Co-Clustering of Word-Document Matrices
comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA)
summary: Spectral co-clustering is a useful tool for discovering latent structure in word-document matrices, but its reliance on singular value decomposition (SVD) can make standard formulations expensive on high-dimensional data. This paper presents two randomized approximations for normalized spectral co-clustering of bipartite text data when the numbers of document and word clusters may differ. The first method uses randomized SVD through random projection, while the second combines partial SVD with element-wise random sampling. Across real-world and synthetic datasets, both methods reduce runtime relative to the full-SVD baseline, but their behavior depends on matrix sparsity. The random projection method is the more reliable approximation across the tested settings, whereas the sampling-based method is most useful on denser matrices and provides limited benefit on already sparse text data. These results show that randomized approximations for spectral co-clustering should be selected according to the underlying structure of the data.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes two randomized approximations for normalized spectral co-clustering of bipartite text data to address the computational expense of SVD on high-dimensional word-document matrices. The random projection method proves more reliable across settings, while sampling-based method benefits denser matrices but offers limited improvement on sparse text data.
AI.motivation: Standard spectral co-clustering relies on singular value decomposition (SVD), which becomes computationally expensive on high-dimensional word-document matrices. There is a need for faster approximations that maintain clustering quality.
AI.method: Two randomized approximations: (1) Randomized SVD through random projection, and (2) Partial SVD combined with element-wise random sampling. Both handle cases where document and word cluster numbers may differ.
AI.result: Both methods reduce runtime relative to full-SVD baseline. Random projection is more reliable across all tested settings. Sampling-based method is most useful on denser matrices but provides limited benefit on already sparse text data.
AI.conclusion: Randomized approximations for spectral co-clustering should be selected according to the underlying structure (sparsity) of the data, not applied uniformly.

title: BinoGen: Scaling egocentric binocular data for embodied visual perception and learning
summary: Embodied visual perception relies on temporally coherent visual experience accumulated through continuous engagement with the environment. However, collecting large-scale egocentric binocular observations together with dense annotations remains costly and difficult. Moreover, visual experience is shaped not only by the environment but also by the embodiment of the observer, including viewing height, field of view, binocular geometry, and motion through the scene. To address these challenges, we present BinoGen, an automated framework for generating large-scale, embodiment-aware egocentric binocular visual experiences in indoor environments. BinoGen jointly models environmental and observer variation through generative scene synthesis, probabilistic object instantiation, appearance randomization, stochastic trajectory generation, and configurable binocular camera setups. The framework produces synchronized binocular videos together with dense multimodal supervision, including depth maps, optical flow, surface normals, semantic maps, object coordinates, and camera poses. Using BinoGen, we construct a dataset comprising more than 20 million annotated images for supervised learning. We demonstrate two complementary utilities of BinoGen. First, incorporating BinoGen data consistently improves real-world visual perception, including depth estimation, object detection, and video object tracking. Second, paired human-inspired and mouse-inspired observations from the same environments enable controlled investigation of how observer embodiment affects perceptual learning. Embodiment-specific adaptation substantially improves performance, while joint training enables a single model to perform competitively across both embodiments. Together, these results demonstrate that large-scale, controllable visual experience can improve embodied perception...

AI.tldr: BinoGen is an automated framework for generating large-scale, embodiment-aware egocentric binocular visual experiences in indoor environments. It produces synchronized binocular videos with dense multimodal annotations (depth, optical flow, normals, semantics, object coordinates, poses) and constructs a dataset of 20+ million annotated images. The framework improves real-world visual perception tasks (depth estimation, object detection, tracking) and enables investigation of how observer embodiment affects perceptual learning.
AI.motivation: Current challenges in embodied visual perception: (1) Collecting large-scale egocentric binocular observations with dense annotations is costly and difficult. (2) Visual experience is shaped not only by the environment but also by the observer's embodiment (viewing height, field of view, binocular geometry, motion through the scene). Existing datasets lack embodiment-aware variation.
AI.method: BinoGen jointly models environmental and observer variation through five components: (1) Generative scene synthesis, (2) Probabilistic object instantiation, (3) Appearance randomization, (4) Stochastic trajectory generation, (5) Configurable binocular camera setups. The framework produces synchronized binocular videos with dense multimodal supervision.
AI.result: 1. Dataset: More than 20 million annotated images generated. 2. Utility 1: Incorporating BinoGen data consistently improves real-world visual perception including depth estimation, object detection, and video object tracking. 3. Utility 2: Paired human-inspired and mouse-inspired observations enable controlled investigation of embodiment effects. Embodiment-specific adaptation substantially improves performance, while joint training enables a single model to perform competitively across both embodiments.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale, controllable visual experience can improve embodied perception. The framework demonstrates that synthetic embodiment-aware data is valuable for both improving downstream visual tasks and studying how observer embodiment affects perceptual learning.

title: An Elementary Expression for Multiple Scattering in Homogeneous Microflake Media
summary: We derive a novel diffuse-like BRDF based on microfacet theory. Its main novelty lies in the fact that it admits an elementary expression for both evaluation and importance sampling, while accounting exactly for all scattering orders under the Smith shadowing assumption. As such, it is the first to settle the question of whether such a construction was possible. In practice, the BRDF produces Lambertian reflectance at normal incidence and progressively concentrates reflected light around the mirror direction as incidence approaches grazing. We showcase this effect by comparing rendering results against Lambertian and state-of-the-art stochastic microfacet BRDFs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel diffuse-like BRDF based on microfacet theory that has a closed-form solution for both evaluation and importance sampling, while exactly accounting for all scattering orders under the Smith shadowing assumption. This is the first such construction, solving a long-standing question in rendering research.
AI.motivation: The authors seek to create a BRDF that combines the best of both worlds: diffuse-like behavior (Lambertian at normal incidence) with the flexibility of microfacet theory. Previous attempts either lacked closed-form solutions or could not account for all scattering orders exactly under the Smith shadowing assumption. This work aims to determine if such a construction is possible and to provide a practical solution.
AI.method: The method derives a new BRDF based on microfacet theory with an elementary (closed-form) expression. This allows for both efficient evaluation and importance sampling. The key breakthrough is that it exactly accounts for all scattering orders under the Smith shadowing assumption - a first in the field.
AI.result: The resulting BRDF exhibits interesting optical behavior: it produces Lambertian reflectance at normal incidence (light hitting head-on) and progressively concentrates reflected light around the mirror direction as incidence approaches grazing angles. The paper includes rendering comparisons against both Lambertian and state-of-the-art stochastic microfacet BRDFs to demonstrate this effect.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that such a construction is indeed possible, settling the open question. The BRDF provides a practical solution that bridges the gap between diffuse and specular rendering, with exact mathematical treatment of multiple scattering under the Smith shadowing model.

title: A Closed-Loop Control Architecture for Reliable Constraint Satisfaction in LLM Text Generation
comment: ICSEA 2026: The Twenty-First International Conference on Software Engineering Advances
summary: Software systems increasingly embed a large language model in features that must satisfy a numeric output constraint, that is, a requirement expressible as a number or an interval and checkable by code, such as a target word count or a target readability grade band. Because such a model is non-deterministic, is configured through natural-language instructions rather than a typed interface, and satisfies a stated requirement only approximately, a single prompt neither reliably meets the target nor preserves the source content. This paper presents and evaluates a closed-loop control architecture for this problem. It has five stages: generate, evaluate, adjust, archive, and analyze. The model is called only to write and to edit text, while deterministic code compares a composite readability value against a target band, rejects any edit that drops source entities, numbers, or keywords, and makes every accept decision. Over 114 single-shot generation jobs and 240 closed-loop runs on four commercial models, single-shot prompting met the target in 21.1 to 31.6 percent of cases and the closed loop in 92.5 to 98.8 percent, within two edit rounds on average and at a recall-based fidelity of 0.92 to 0.93; the two models common to both settings show the same effect. Because the controller optimizes the value on which success is scored, the result establishes reproducible control over a declared, computable metric and not validated human difficulty. The transferable practice is to declare the acceptance condition as code, bound the model to local edits, and gate every edit on a content check.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a closed-loop control architecture for constraining large language model outputs to meet numeric constraints (e.g., word count, readability grade bands). The system uses a five-stage pipeline (generate, evaluate, adjust, archive, analyze) where deterministic code evaluates outputs against targets while preserving source content. Experiments on four commercial models show the closed-loop approach achieves 92.5-98.8% target accuracy compared to 21.1-31.6% for single-shot prompting.
AI.motivation: Large language models are increasingly embedded in software features requiring numeric output constraints (target word count, readability grade). However, LLMs are non-deterministic, configured via natural language, and only approximately satisfy requirements. Single prompts cannot reliably meet numeric targets while preserving source content, creating a practical engineering challenge.
AI.method: The authors propose a closed-loop control architecture with five stages: (1) generate - model produces initial output, (2) evaluate - deterministic code checks composite readability against target band, (3) adjust - model makes local edits, (4) archive - store results, (5) analyze - process metrics. Key design principles: (1) model only writes/edits text, (2) deterministic code handles evaluation, (3) rejects edits dropping source entities/numbers/keywords, (4) code gates every accept decision.
AI.result: Over 114 single-shot jobs and 240 closed-loop runs on four commercial models: single-shot prompting met targets in 21.1-31.6% of cases; closed-loop achieved 92.5-98.8% within two edit rounds on average, with recall-based fidelity of 0.92-0.93. Two models tested in both settings showed consistent improvements.
AI.conclusion: The closed-loop controller achieves reproducible control over declared, computable metrics (not validated human difficulty). The transferable practice is to: (1) declare acceptance conditions as code, (2) bound model to local edits, (3) gate every edit on content checks. This establishes a robust engineering approach for LLM-powered features requiring numeric constraints.

title: RGS: Reflection-aware Gaussian Splatting via Learning Geometry Continuity for Reflective Objects
summary: Gaussian Splatting has significantly improved the quality of novel view synthesis with explicit Gaussian representation. However, we observed that existing 3D Gaussian Splatting methods (3DGS) often suffer from surface collapse issues on reflective regions, and thus produce inferior geometry and low-quality specular. In this work, we propose a physically-based deferred rendering framework, named Reflection-aware Gaussian Splatting (RGS), that can accurately model specular regions and improve novel view synthesis performance. Specifically, we found that a powerful 3D foundation model can provide a strong 3D geometric prior to foster correct geometric modeling. Based on this, we propose a cross-view shape consistency regularization to regularize the geometry surface with the large model prior and cross-view constraints. In this manner, our RGS can produce smoother geometric surfaces on reflective regions while reducing geometric hollows. To further improve rendering results on reflective regions, we present a reflection-aware densification strategy that is designed to capture specular variations across various views. With this strategy, our RGS is able to render novel views of objects in higher quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate our method consistently renders high-quality reflective objects, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: RGS proposes a physically-based deferred rendering framework for Gaussian Splatting that addresses surface collapse issues on reflective regions by using 3D foundation model priors and cross-view shape consistency regularization, combined with a reflection-aware densification strategy.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting methods suffer from surface collapse issues on reflective regions, leading to inferior geometry and low-quality specular rendering. This limits the quality of novel view synthesis for reflective objects.
AI.method:
1) Physically-based deferred rendering framework for accurate specular modeling
2) 3D foundation model provides geometric prior
3) Cross-view shape consistency regularization to regularize geometry with large model prior and cross-view constraints
4) Reflection-aware densification strategy to capture specular variations across views
AI.result: RGS produces smoother geometric surfaces on reflective regions, reduces geometric hollows, and enables high-quality novel view rendering of reflective objects.
AI.conclusion: The method consistently renders high-quality reflective objects and achieves state-of-the-art performance on novel view synthesis tasks.

title: CircleMatch: Prototype Matching with Circular Temporal Statistics for Tiny Keyword Spotting
summary: Keyword spotting (KWS), the task of identifying predefined words in speech, is a core capability of voice-enabled devices. Achieving high KWS accuracy under tight parameter budgets across different vocabulary sizes remains challenging. We present CircleMatch, a matching framework enabling KWS with very few parameters. Its encoder independently compresses frequency bands and fuses them into frame features. These features are then matched against learned class-specific prototypes to produce temporal response curves. Parameter-free circular aggregation encodes time as angles and summarizes response distributions and relative timing for classification. We develop four tiny variants, Circle-D4, Circle-D8, Circle-D16, and Circle-D32, ranging from approximately 1k to 7k parameters in the 12-class setting. Experiments with multiple random seeds on Speech Commands v1/v2 and the English and Spanish Micro subsets of the Multilingual Spoken Words Corpus demonstrate competitive accuracy with tiny models. Our qualitative analysis further suggests approximate shift equivariance of prototype responses and adaptation to temporal compression. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/ora942878/CircleMatch.

AI.tldr: CircleMatch is a ultra-lightweight keyword spotting framework that uses a matching-based approach with prototype matching and circular aggregation to achieve competitive accuracy with only 1k-7k parameters.
AI.motivation: Keyword spotting is essential for voice-enabled devices, but achieving high accuracy under tight parameter budgets (especially across different vocabulary sizes) remains challenging. Existing methods typically require substantial computational resources.
AI.method: CircleMatch uses: 1) A frequency band encoder that independently compresses frequency bands and fuses them into frame features; 2) Class-specific prototypes for matching against frame features to produce temporal response curves; 3) Parameter-free circular aggregation that encodes time as angles and summarizes response distributions and relative timing for classification.
AI.result: Four tiny variants (Circle-D4, Circle-D8, Circle-D16, Circle-D32) with 1k-7k parameters achieve competitive accuracy on Speech Commands v1/v2 and Multilingual Spoken Words Corpus (English and Spanish subsets). The approach shows approximate shift equivariance of prototype responses and adapts to temporal compression.
AI.conclusion: CircleMatch demonstrates that matching-based approaches can achieve competitive KWS accuracy with extremely few parameters, making it suitable for ultra-low-power embedded devices. The circular aggregation effectively encodes temporal information without additional parameters.

title: What Do Current Systematic Generalization Tasks Miss? A Reasoning-Centered Analysis
summary: Systematic generalization, the ability to solve novel problems by recombining known atomic elements, is central to human intelligence but difficult to study rigorously under controlled settings. Existing studies therefore rely on simplifications such as approximately linear action composition, productivity-based tests, and action-explicit goals, which make systematic generalization easier to study but omit some essential aspects of this capability. To characterize what these simplifications miss, we adopt a reasoning-centered lens and introduce TranSGrid, a testbed that brings deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning together within a unified task. Experiments with seven Transformers on 4,800 TranSGrid instances show that all models perform much worse on TranSGrid than on a held-out test set: the largest model solves 79.6% of the test set, but only 55.3% of TranSGrid and 15.8% of the hardest subset. The gap remains within the training length range, showing that productivity alone is not sufficient to evaluate systematic generalization. Additionally, we reintroduce the other two simplifications into TranSGrid: one variant makes actions compose almost linearly (reducing the inductive demand), the other makes goals action-explicit (reducing the abductive one). In both, solve rates return to roughly the test set level, showing that either simplification alone is enough to reduce TranSGrid to an ordinary held-out test set. Together, our results show that existing tasks reduce either or both of the inductive and abductive demands, and that comprehensively measuring systematic generalization requires a task that involves all three forms of reasoning.

AI.tldr: TranSGrid is a new testbed that combines deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning to comprehensively measure systematic generalization in AI models. Experiments on 7 Transformers reveal significant performance gaps: the largest model achieves 79.6% on held-out test sets but only 55.3% on TranSGrid and 15.8% on the hardest subset. The study shows that existing simplifications (linear action composition and action-explicit goals) reduce either inductive or abductive demands, making tasks easier but missing essential aspects of systematic generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing studies on systematic generalization rely on simplifications (linear action composition, productivity-based tests, action-explicit goals) that make the problem easier to study but omit essential aspects of this capability. There was a need for a comprehensive testbed that captures all three forms of reasoning (deductive, inductive, abductive) to properly evaluate systematic generalization.
AI.method: The authors introduce TranSGrid, a unified task that integrates deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning. They tested seven Transformer models on 4,800 TranSGrid instances. They also conducted ablation studies by reintroducing two simplifications: (1) making actions compose almost linearly (reducing inductive demand), and (2) making goals action-explicit (reducing abductive demand).
AI.result: All models perform significantly worse on TranSGrid than on held-out test sets. The largest model solves 79.6% of the test set, but only 55.3% of TranSGrid and 15.8% of the hardest subset. The performance gap persists within the training length range. When either simplification is reintroduced, solve rates return to roughly test set level, demonstrating that each simplification alone reduces TranSGrid to an ordinary held-out test set.
AI.conclusion: Existing systematic generalization tasks reduce either or both of the inductive and abductive demands. To comprehensively measure systematic generalization, a task must involve all three forms of reasoning (deductive, inductive, and abductive). Productivity alone is insufficient for evaluating systematic generalization.

title: Radio-Frequency Convolutional Neural Networks
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary Information: 50 pages, 31 figures, 1 table
summary: Running artificial intelligence (AI) models directly on edge devices such as smartphones, wearables, and drones offers low latency, pervasive scalability, and data privacy, but these devices rarely carry the computing capability that modern neural networks demand. Edge accelerators have been developed in response, yet each adds computing hardware to devices already constrained in size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C). An alternative lies in what these devices already carry: the frequency mixer in every wireless radio multiplies signals in time, natively performing convolution in the frequency domain. Here we introduce radio-frequency convolutional neural networks (RF-CNNs), which repurpose existing communication hardware for CNN inference. Multi-channel convolutions are mapped onto frequency tones for a passive mixer to execute in a single pass. We experimentally demonstrate that RF-CNN runs deep CNNs up to 26.4 million parameters and nine layers from classification of wireless signals and images to controllable image generation, close to full-precision performance. Because the weights arrive over the air and the analog hardware is shared with communication, the edge device spends energy only on data preparation and readout-down to 0.72 femtojoules per multiply-accumulate, two orders of magnitude less than it would cost on an added digital processor. These results suggest that deployed wireless infrastructure can bring efficient, state-of-the-art AI inference to the billions of devices it already connects.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces radio-frequency convolutional neural networks (RF-CNNs), which repurpose existing wireless radio hardware (frequency mixers) for CNN inference, enabling efficient deep learning on edge devices without additional hardware.
AI.motivation: Edge devices lack the computing capability for modern neural networks, while adding accelerators increases size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C). The authors propose leveraging existing communication hardware—the frequency mixer in wireless radios—as a solution.
AI.method: Multi-channel convolutions are mapped onto frequency tones, allowing a passive mixer to execute convolutions in a single pass in the frequency domain. Weights arrive over the air, and analog hardware is shared with communication.
AI.result: RF-CNN successfully runs deep CNNs with up to 26.4 million parameters and nine layers across tasks including wireless signal classification, image classification, and controllable image generation, achieving close to full-precision performance. Energy consumption is as low as 0.72 femtojoules per multiply-accumulate—two orders of magnitude lower than digital processors.
AI.conclusion: Deployed wireless infrastructure can deliver efficient, state-of-the-art AI inference to billions of edge devices by repurposing existing radio hardware, eliminating the need for additional computing hardware while achieving massive energy savings.

title: SAGG: Sample-Adaptive Gradient Gating for Robust Multimodal Learning under Heterogeneous Corruption
summary: Multimodal gradient balancing methods modulate encoder gradients with a shared scalar per modality, implicitly assuming that corruption is uniform across the training batch. In practice, corruption is sample-heterogeneous: within a single mini-batch, different samples may have different modalities corrupted. We prove that under this heterogeneous corruption model, any batch-level sample-agnostic linear estimator with a shared modulation parameter incurs an irreducible bias with respect to the clean-data gradient, and that sample-level all-or-nothing gating is the unique unbiased strategy within a natural distribution-free estimator class. Motivated by this result, we propose Sample-Adaptive Gradient Gating (SAGG), which makes a binary retain-or-discard decision per sample via an online feature-norm quality test and incorporates a truncation mechanism for variance control. We prove that SAGG-based SGD converges at the standard O(1/sqrt(T)) rate to stationary points of the clean loss without a corruption-dependent error floor, and derive a certified robustness radius for the independent-encoder architecture that connects per-modality Lipschitz constants to the classification margin. Experiments on Kinetics-Sounds and UCF-101 under Gaussian noise injection, partial modality missing, and natural contribution imbalance show that SAGG consistently outperforms ten existing methods, with the largest gains in high-corruption regimes where batch-level bias is most severe.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses multimodal learning under heterogeneous modality corruption, where different samples in a batch have different modalities corrupted. The authors prove that existing batch-level gradient balancing methods incur irreducible bias under this realistic corruption model, and propose Sample-Adaptive Gradient Gating (SAGG) - a sample-level gating mechanism that makes per-sample retain-or-discard decisions using feature-norm quality testing. SAGG achieves O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence to clean loss stationary points without corruption-dependent error floor.
AI.motivation: Multimodal gradient balancing methods assume uniform corruption across training batches, but real-world corruption is sample-heterogeneous - different samples within a mini-batch have different modalities corrupted. This mismatch creates irreducible bias in existing methods.
AI.method: The authors theoretically prove that under heterogeneous corruption, any batch-level sample-agnostic linear estimator with shared modulation parameter has irreducible bias. They then propose Sample-Adaptive Gradient Gating (SAGG), which: (1) makes binary retain-or-discard decisions per sample via online feature-norm quality test, (2) incorporates truncation mechanism for variance control, and (3) uses independent-encoder architecture.
AI.result: SAGG outperforms ten existing methods on Kinetics-Sounds and UCF-101 under Gaussian noise injection, partial modality missing, and natural contribution imbalance, with largest gains in high-corruption regimes.
AI.conclusion: Sample-level all-or-nothing gating is the unique unbiased strategy within natural distribution-free estimator classes. SAGG achieves standard O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate to stationary points of clean loss without corruption-dependent error floor, with certified robustness radius connecting per-modality Lipschitz constants to classification margin.

title: S4R: Scaling for Rigid-Body Interpenetration Resolution
comment: ACM Transactions on Graphics 45(6), Article 197 (SIGGRAPH Asia 2026). Project page: https://frank-zy-dou.github.io/projects/S4R/index.html
summary: Rigid-body interpenetration frequently occurs in procedurally assembled and generated scenes and must be removed before downstream applications such as physical simulation. We present S4R (Scaling for Rigid-Body Interpenetration Resolution), a scale-continuation method for static interpenetration repair. S4R first uniformly shrinks each body about a fixed reference center to a small initial scale, at which the layout is penetration-free, and then restores full scale through a sequence of minimum-norm convex contact quadratic programs (QPs) that target the linearized separation margin during continuation. Resolution thereby replaces one deep correction with a sequence of shallow-contact subproblems. A conservative scale-event bound and frozen-witness gap predictions cut the number of exact mesh queries; the continuation then ends with a full-scale evaluator check and bounded tail refinement. We evaluate S4R on Kubric, HY3D-Bench, and Thingi10K using a shared mesh-level evaluator and a unified per-scene timing protocol. In the main comparisons on all three benchmarks, up to N=5000 bodies, S4R reaches zero reported penetration with displacement that stays small and nearly independent of scene size, and at the lowest wall time within each hardware tier among the compared methods. A GPU implementation extends these results to large-scale scenes. Our code and data can be found on our project page: https://frank-zy-dou.github.io/projects/S4R/index.html.

AI.tldr: S4R is a scale-continuation method for resolving rigid-body interpenetration in procedurally generated scenes. It shrinks bodies to a penetration-free state, then restores scale through a sequence of shallow-contact quadratic programs, achieving zero penetration with minimal displacement and fastest runtime among compared methods.
AI.motivation: Rigid-body interpenetration frequently occurs in procedurally assembled and generated scenes and must be removed before downstream applications like physical simulation. Existing methods struggle with deep penetrations and large-scale scenes.
AI.method: Scale-continuation approach: (1) Uniformly shrink each body about a fixed reference center to a small initial scale where the layout is penetration-free; (2) Restore full scale through a sequence of minimum-norm convex contact quadratic programs (QPs) targeting linearized separation margin during continuation; (3) Use conservative scale-event bound and frozen-witness gap predictions to reduce exact mesh queries; (4) End with full-scale evaluator check and bounded tail refinement.
AI.result: On Kubric, HY3D-Bench, and Thingi10K benchmarks with up to N=5000 bodies: achieves zero reported penetration, displacement stays small and nearly independent of scene size, and lowest wall time within each hardware tier among compared methods. GPU implementation extends results to large-scale scenes.
AI.conclusion: S4R provides an efficient and effective solution for rigid-body interpenetration resolution in large-scale procedurally generated scenes, combining scale continuation with convex optimization to achieve superior performance in both accuracy and speed.

title: EviRCA: Decoupling Evidence Extraction from Reasoning for Microservice Root-Cause Analysis
summary: Root-cause analysis (RCA) is a critical yet labor-intensive task for maintaining modern microservice systems, making it an attractive target for large language models (LLMs). Recent agentic approaches allow an LLM to iteratively explore raw telemetry by generating and executing code, asking a single model to simultaneously retrieve evidence, localize faults, and infer root causes over large volumes of heterogeneous telemetry, which leads to high computational cost, unstable behavior, and limited diagnostic accuracy. However, raw telemetry consists of numeric metrics, structured traces, and machine-generated logs that are not directly suitable for LLM processing. We present EviRCA, a framework for LLM-based RCA that decouples deterministic evidence extraction from LLM reasoning. A system-agnostic extraction stage converts raw metrics, traces, and logs into a compact set of faithful multimodal evidence cards, while the LLM reasons only over these structured observations through a small set of predefined read-only tools, without accessing raw telemetry or executing code. We evaluate EviRCA on OpenRCA, a benchmark built from real, heterogeneous telemetry across three enterprise systems. EviRCA achieves a correct rate of 40.6%-43.9% across two different LLMs, substantially outperforming prior OpenRCA baselines that achieve up to 15.2%, while reducing token consumption by 15-26x and execution time by 3-20x. Moreover, EviRCA solves hard cases requiring simultaneous reasoning over time, components, and root causes, a setting where previous approaches reported near-zero performance. Our process-level failure analysis further shows that the bottleneck lies in judging the evidence that the extraction stage has already surfaced, rather than searching for it, suggesting that the effectiveness of LLM-based RCA depends heavily on the quality of evidence extraction.

AI.tldr: EviRCA is an LLM-based root-cause analysis framework for microservice systems that decouples deterministic evidence extraction from LLM reasoning. It converts raw telemetry (metrics, traces, logs) into structured evidence cards, allowing the LLM to reason only over these compact observations without accessing raw data or executing code.
AI.motivation: Root-cause analysis in modern microservice systems is critical but labor-intensive. Existing agentic LLM approaches require a single model to simultaneously retrieve evidence, localize faults, and infer root causes over large volumes of heterogeneous telemetry, leading to high computational cost, unstable behavior, and limited diagnostic accuracy. Raw telemetry (numeric metrics, structured traces, logs) is not directly suitable for LLM processing.
AI.method: EviRCA uses a two-stage approach: (1) A system-agnostic extraction stage converts raw metrics, traces, and logs into compact multimodal evidence cards; (2) The LLM reasons only over these structured observations through predefined read-only tools, without accessing raw telemetry or executing code. Evaluated on OpenRCA benchmark built from real heterogeneous telemetry across three enterprise systems.
AI.result: EviRCA achieves a correct rate of 40.6%-43.9% across two different LLMs, substantially outperforming prior OpenRCA baselines (up to 15.2%). It reduces token consumption by 15-26x and execution time by 3-20x. It solves hard cases requiring simultaneous reasoning over time, components, and root causes where previous approaches had near-zero performance.
AI.conclusion: The effectiveness of LLM-based RCA depends heavily on the quality of evidence extraction. The bottleneck lies in judging the evidence that the extraction stage has already surfaced, rather than searching for it. The decoupled approach significantly improves performance while reducing computational cost.

title: Seeing Abnormal from Normal: Glomerular Abnormality in Representations of Normal Renal Morphology
summary: Fine-grained evaluation of glomerular pathology must distinguish normal glomeruli from abnormalities such as global and segmental glomerulosclerosis, obsolescent, ischemic, solidified, disappearing, and atubular glomeruli. Supervised classification requires labeled examples of every category, which is impractical when subtypes are rare or absent from the training cohort. One-class anomaly detection offers an alternative by modeling normal data and scoring deviations, allowing previously unseen abnormalities to be detected. We use the frozen residual U-Net backbone of Omni-Seg, pretrained to segment structurally normal renal primitives without abnormal-subtype labels. We propose NoRDeC (Normal-Reference Detection and Characterization), a framework combining Mahalanobis normal-reference scoring with layer-wise representation analysis to determine whether and where glomerular pathology is encoded, how spatial aggregation affects detection, and whether abnormalities alter inter-layer relationships differently. Using glomerular images from two institutions, we evaluate backbone layers and aggregation strategies, compare NoRDeC with PaDiM and PatchCore, and analyze representations using centered kernel alignment (CKA). Layer 4 with Center-70 aggregation achieved a pooled AUROC of $0.926\pm0.013$. NoRDeC achieved the highest AUROC in six of seven abnormality categories and in the pooled analysis, while CKA suggested subtype-dependent changes in inter-layer relationships not captured by anomaly scores alone. The normal-reference model is fitted using only normal glomeruli; abnormality labels are used for configuration selection, evaluation, and grouping in the representation analysis. These results show that a frozen renal feature extractor can support both detection and representation-level characterization of glomerular abnormalities without using abnormal examples to fit the detector.

AI.tldr: NoRDeC is a one-class anomaly detection framework for fine-grained evaluation of glomerular pathology using a frozen pretrained U-Net backbone. It uses Mahalanobis normal-reference scoring with layer-wise representation analysis to detect abnormalities without training on abnormal examples. Achieved AUROC of 0.926±0.013 and outperformed PaDiM and PatchCore in 6/7 abnormality categories.
AI.motivation: Fine-grained glomerular pathology evaluation requires distinguishing multiple abnormality types, but supervised classification needs labeled examples of every category - impractical for rare subtypes. One-class anomaly detection offers an alternative by modeling only normal data and scoring deviations.
AI.method: NoRDeC combines Mahalanobis normal-reference scoring with layer-wise representation analysis. Uses frozen residual U-Net backbone from Omni-Seg (pretrained on normal renal primitives only). Evaluates different backbone layers and aggregation strategies (Center-70). Uses Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) to analyze inter-layer relationships.
AI.result: Layer 4 with Center-70 aggregation achieved pooled AUROC of 0.926±0.013. NoRDeC outperformed PaDiM and PatchCore in 6 of 7 abnormality categories and in pooled analysis. CKA analysis revealed subtype-dependent changes in inter-layer relationships not captured by anomaly scores alone.
AI.conclusion: A frozen renal feature extractor can support both detection and representation-level characterization of glomerular abnormalities without using abnormal examples to fit the detector, enabling detection of previously unseen abnormalities.

title: Multi-Dimensional Prosody Judgment For Live Streaming Speech Synthesis
summary: Evaluating live streaming speech synthesis (TTS) requires assessing fine-grained, highly expressive prosody such as emotion, intonation, and energy which traditional MOS predictors fail to capture. While proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs) like Gemini can evaluate these aspects, they are too costly for massive inference and reinforcement learning feedback. To address this, we first introduce Live-ProsodyJudge (LPJ), a cost-effective pairwise evaluator distilled from Gemini into Qwen3-Omni. However, we identify a critical flaw in standard multi-dimensional evaluation: verdict coupling. The judge tends to lazily align all individual dimension scores with its overall preference, collapsing a rich multi-dimensional rubric into a single preference bit. To resolve this, we further propose Decoupled-Live-ProsodyJudge (D-LPJ). D-LPJ eliminates the overall verdict target to prevent blind following, masks uncertain pair-dimensions during Supervised Fine-Tuning(SFT), and introduces a novel span-local GRPO strategy that applies normalized advantages strictly to their corresponding rationale spans. Evaluated on highly curated human-annotated test sets, 10 sample balanced-order LPJ achieves higher point accuracy than a single Gemini call, while D-LPJ successfully produces independent,decoupled dimension judgments. Furthermore, in a Best-of-8 TTS candidate selection tournament, the LPJ-selected utterance falls within the human top-3 in 85.29% of high-confidence cases, demonstrating its efficacy for fine-grained TTS preference optimization.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of evaluating fine-grained prosody in live streaming speech synthesis (TTS), which traditional MOS predictors fail to capture. The authors propose Live-ProsodyJudge (LPJ), a cost-effective pairwise evaluator distilled from Gemini into Qwen3-Omni, and identify a critical flaw called "verdict coupling" in standard multi-dimensional evaluation. To resolve this, they propose Decoupled-Live-ProsodyJudge (D-LPJ) with novel training strategies including span-local GRPO.
AI.motivation: Traditional MOS predictors cannot assess fine-grained, highly expressive prosody (emotion, intonation, energy) in live streaming TTS. While proprietary LLMs like Gemini can evaluate these aspects, they are prohibitively expensive for massive inference and reinforcement learning feedback applications.
AI.method: The authors first introduce Live-ProsodyJudge (LPJ), a cost-effective pairwise evaluator distilled from Gemini into Qwen3-Omni. To address verdict coupling (where judges lazily align all dimension scores with overall preference), they propose Decoupled-Live-ProsodyJudge (D-LPJ) with three key innovations: (1) eliminating overall verdict target to prevent blind following, (2) masking uncertain pair-dimensions during Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and (3) introducing span-local GRPO strategy that applies normalized advantages strictly to corresponding rationale spans.
AI.result: LPJ with 10 sample balanced-order achieves higher point accuracy than a single Gemini call. D-LPJ successfully produces independent, decoupled dimension judgments. In a Best-of-8 TTS candidate selection tournament, LPJ-selected utterances fall within human top-3 in 85.29% of high-confidence cases, demonstrating efficacy for fine-grained TTS preference optimization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed LPJ and D-LPJ provide cost-effective alternatives to proprietary LLMs for evaluating fine-grained prosody in live streaming TTS. D-LPJ successfully addresses verdict coupling through decoupled training, enabling independent multi-dimensional judgments while maintaining high accuracy in preference optimization tasks.

title: Characterizing Web Search by Conversational LLM Agents: From Search Decisions and Strategies to Results and Responses
summary: Conversational LLM agents increasingly rely on Web search, yet the end-to-end lifecycle of agentic search remains poorly understood. We present the first study of Web search across four major conversational platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and DeepSeek), combining real-world user interactions (invivo) with controlled experiments using the same platform's models by their APIs (invitro). We investigate the quality of agentic decisions to invoke Web search, their strategies to formulate queries, the potential domain preferences in the search results they receive, and the choices they make when transforming search results into grounded responses. We find that Web-search decisions vary substantially across platforms and models, while more frequent Web-search invocation does not necessarily yield better response quality. We further show that conversational agents employ different complex querying strategies and that platform specific search engines return search results from their preferred domains. Finally, although responses are largely grounded in search results, some claims rely on uncited search results, raising concerns about attribution and reliability. Our findings have important implications for the design of future AI agents and Web search tools optimized for conversational retrieval.

AI.tldr: First comprehensive study of Web search across four major conversational LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek), combining real-world user interactions with controlled experiments. The study reveals substantial variations in search decisions, querying strategies, and attribution issues across platforms.
AI.motivation: The end-to-end lifecycle of agentic search remains poorly understood despite increasing reliance on Web search by conversational LLM agents.
AI.method: Combined in vivo (real-world user interactions) and in vitro (controlled experiments using same platform APIs) approaches across four major conversational platforms to investigate: search invocation decisions, query formulation strategies, domain preferences in search results, and response grounding choices.
AI.result: Web-search decisions vary substantially across platforms and models; more frequent search invocation does not necessarily yield better response quality. Conversational agents employ different complex querying strategies, and platform-specific search engines return results from preferred domains. While responses are largely grounded in search results, some claims rely on uncited search results, raising attribution and reliability concerns.
AI.conclusion: Findings have important implications for the design of future AI agents and Web search tools optimized for conversational retrieval, highlighting the need for better attribution mechanisms and platform-independent evaluation metrics.

title: Learning-Induced Dynamical Transition in Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Learning in recurrent neural networks can fundamentally reshape their underlying dynamics, transforming initially chaotic activity into stable task-dependent behavior. We develop a non-equilibrium dynamical mean-field theory(DMFT) to describe this transition during learning. We show that a slow feedback-driven learning process generates an evolving effective feedback strength that drives the network through a transition from chaotic to stable dynamics defined by a bifurcation of the DMFT solution. By deriving the two-time correlation function throughout learning, we identify a critical feedback strength and a corresponding learning rate dependent critical time separating these regimes. The transition arises from the progressive deformation of an effective dynamical landscape by the growing learned feedback structure. Starting from the untrained state, the theory predicts the time evolution of the network output during training and shows quantitative agreement with numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a non-equilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) to describe how learning transforms recurrent neural networks from chaotic to stable dynamics. The theory identifies a critical feedback strength and learning rate-dependent critical time that separates these regimes, with quantitative agreement to simulations.
AI.motivation: Understanding how learning in recurrent neural networks transforms initially chaotic activity into stable task-dependent behavior, and developing a theoretical framework to describe this transition.
AI.method: Non-equilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) to derive the two-time correlation function throughout learning, identifying a critical feedback strength and learning rate-dependent critical time.
AI.result: The theory predicts a bifurcation in the DMFT solution that defines the transition from chaotic to stable dynamics. This transition arises from the progressive deformation of an effective dynamical landscape by the growing learned feedback structure. The theory shows quantitative agreement with numerical simulations.
AI.conclusion: The learning process drives the network through a transition from chaotic to stable dynamics via a slow feedback-driven process that generates an evolving effective feedback strength. The theory successfully predicts the time evolution of network output during training.

title: PART: Learning 3D Part Assembly and Retrieval with Transformers
comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers. 11 pages, 12 figures. Project page: https://iambrc.github.io/PART-project-page/
summary: 3D assembly is fundamental to modern manufacturing and digital content creation. In this paper, we present PART, a unified transformer-based framework for 3D part retrieval and assembly: given a target shape and a part library, PART automatically selects the appropriate parts and predicts their 6-DoF poses to reconstruct the target. While prior work has achieved impressive progress on assembling a pre-defined set of parts, this more practical retrieval-based setting remains largely unexplored. The task faces three key challenges: (i) a combinatorially explosive search space that grows exponentially with library size; (ii) variable-length outputs, as different targets require different numbers of parts; and (iii) continuous 6-DoF pose estimation for part assembly. To address these, we formulate retrieval and assembly as a set prediction problem and design a novel transformer-based framework that retrieves parts and regresses their poses with variable-length output. Additionally, we exploit the duality between part pose estimation and target segmentation through joint training and a novel segmentation-enhanced optimization module. Finally, We curate a large-scale dataset of 80K+ shapes, and the results show that PART generalizes to scene layouts, image targets, and real-world scans. Project Page: https://iambrc.github.io/PART-project-page/.

AI.tldr: PART is a unified transformer-based framework for 3D part retrieval and assembly that selects appropriate parts from a library and predicts their 6-DoF poses to reconstruct target shapes. It formulates retrieval and assembly as a set prediction problem with variable-length output, addressing challenges of combinatorial search space, variable outputs, and continuous pose estimation through joint training with segmentation.
AI.motivation: While prior work has achieved progress on assembling pre-defined parts, the more practical retrieval-based setting (selecting from a large part library) remains largely unexplored. This setting is fundamental to modern manufacturing and digital content creation.
AI.method: The paper proposes: (1) Formulating retrieval and assembly as a set prediction problem; (2) A novel transformer-based framework that retrieves parts and regresses poses with variable-length output; (3) Exploiting duality between part pose estimation and target segmentation through joint training; (4) A segmentation-enhanced optimization module.
AI.result: PART generalizes to scene layouts, image targets, and real-world scans. The method is evaluated on a large-scale dataset of 80K+ shapes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed unified transformer framework successfully addresses the retrieval-based 3D assembly problem, handling combinatorial search spaces, variable-length outputs, and continuous 6-DoF pose estimation through innovative set prediction and joint segmentation-pose training.

title: HapCiD: Detecting API-related Compatibility Issues in OpenHarmony Apps
summary: OpenHarmony, an emerging open-source mobile platform, is rapidly gaining attention in the mobile development community. Its fast-evolving Software Development Kit (SDK) introduces numerous Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to boost developer productivity but inevitably introduces compatibility challenges, an issue well known from platforms like Android. However, existing compatibility analysis tools are ineffective for OpenHarmony due to its newly introduced ArkTS programming language and the lack of a mature behavioral model to capture app execution semantics. To bridge this gap, we present HapCiD, an open-source tool for automatically detecting API-related compatibility issues in OpenHarmony apps. Applied to 4,478 apps, HapCiD successfully detects 2,040 compatibility issues across 163 apps with 100 percent accuracy. Based on these findings, we conduct a comprehensive study of compatibility issues, categorizing their types, examining existing mitigation strategies, and proposing future improvements.

AI.tldr: HapCiD is an open-source tool for detecting API-related compatibility issues in OpenHarmony apps, addressing challenges unique to this emerging platform due to its newly introduced ArkTS programming language. Applied to 4,478 apps, it achieved 100% accuracy in detecting 2,040 issues across 163 apps.
AI.motivation: OpenHarmony is a rapidly evolving open-source mobile platform that introduces numerous APIs to boost developer productivity, but this creates compatibility challenges similar to those seen on Android. Existing compatibility analysis tools are ineffective for OpenHarmony because it uses the newly introduced ArkTS programming language and lacks a mature behavioral model to capture app execution semantics.
AI.method: The paper presents HapCiD, an open-source tool for automatically detecting API-related compatibility issues in OpenHarmony apps. The tool was applied to analyze 4,478 apps to identify compatibility issues.
AI.result: HapCiD successfully detected 2,040 compatibility issues across 163 apps with 100 percent accuracy. The study provides a comprehensive analysis categorizing the types of compatibility issues found and examining existing mitigation strategies.
AI.conclusion: The paper proposes future improvements based on the findings, contributing to the understanding of API compatibility challenges in emerging mobile platforms like OpenHarmony.

title: Efficient Unified Multimodal Understanding (EUMU): Winning Solution for the MUMU Track at the 8th LSVOS Challenge
summary: The Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding (MUMU) Challenge requires a single efficient model to jointly perform multi-concept image tagging, open-vocabulary object detection, and image captioning. We present Efficient Unified Multimodal Understanding (EUMU), the winning solution for the MUMU Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge. EUMU builds on a shared pretrained multimodal model, using its prompt-based capabilities for detection and captioning and training lightweight heads on shared visual features to predict quality, scene, and event tags. Rather than treating the three tasks independently, EUMU applies task-aware inference refinement by reusing task outputs as cross-task cues. For detection, caption cues help recover objects missed by the initial detection. For captioning, detection cues help refine the caption to better reflect the detected objects. For tagging, image statistics refine quality predictions, while caption and detection cues refine scene and event predictions. This design unifies all three tasks within a single model while satisfying the challenge's resource constraints. EUMU contains 239.169M parameters, requires 23.947 GFLOPs, uses 4.5 GB of peak inference memory, and achieves a final challenge score of 17.3409. Code and models are available at https://github.com/Dayoung-Kil/EUMU.

AI.tldr: EUMU is the winning solution for the MUMU Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge, presenting a single efficient model that jointly performs multi-concept image tagging, open-vocabulary object detection, and image captioning.
AI.motivation: The MUMU Challenge requires a single efficient model to jointly perform multi-concept image tagging, open-vocabulary object detection, and image captioning while satisfying strict resource constraints.
AI.method: EUMU builds on a shared pretrained multimodal model, leveraging its prompt-based capabilities for detection and captioning. Lightweight heads are trained on shared visual features to predict quality, scene, and event tags. The key innovation is task-aware inference refinement, where task outputs are reused as cross-task cues: caption cues help recover missed objects in detection, detection cues refine captions, and image statistics/caption/detection cues refine tag predictions.
AI.result: EUMU achieves a final challenge score of 17.3409 with 239.169M parameters, 23.947 GFLOPs computational requirement, and 4.5 GB peak inference memory.
AI.conclusion: EUMU successfully unifies three complex vision-language tasks within a single efficient model while meeting the challenge's resource constraints, demonstrating the effectiveness of task-aware inference refinement with cross-task cue reuse.

title: Music Hallucination in Audio-Language Models: A Hierarchical Formulation and Empirical Study
summary: Audio-language models increasingly generate confident music descriptions that are unsupported by the input audio. We present, to our knowledge, the first music-specific, layer-wise, multi-paradigm empirical study of hallucination in audio-language models and formulate it as a hierarchical perceptual grounding failure across five layers: sound events, temporal properties, tonal attributes, style, and emotion. We introduce MuseDiag, a multi-paradigm diagnostic framework with contradiction-based verification, and evaluate nine models (four open-source and five closed-source). We find that (1) vocal misperception is a universal weakness across all nine models, tonal perception is a major axis of architectural differentiation, and Audio-Flamingo-3 remains the stable leader while substantial reordering below it reveals paradigm-specific vulnerability profiles; (2) affirmative bias, generation-mode effects, and layer-specific perceptual limitations are each empirically associated with the observed patterns, with convergent evidence from multiple analyses rather than strict causal attribution; and (3) our two training-free mitigation methods, Audio-Dependency-Aware Decoding for Music (ADD-M) and Taxonomy-Guided Perceptual Anchoring (TPA), can reduce hallucination in probing, but their gains vary by model and often do not carry over to free-form generation, showing that music hallucination mitigation must be evaluated across paradigms.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first music-specific, layer-wise study of hallucination in audio-language models, introducing MuseDiag - a multi-paradigm diagnostic framework. The study evaluates nine models and identifies vocal misperception as a universal weakness, with tonal perception as a key architectural differentiator. Two training-free mitigation methods (ADD-M and TPA) are proposed, though their effectiveness varies across models and generation paradigms.
AI.motivation: Audio-language models increasingly generate confident but unsupported music descriptions, representing a significant problem in AI-generated content. Prior research on hallucination in multimodal models has not specifically addressed music, which has unique perceptual dimensions (sound events, temporal properties, tonal attributes, style, and emotion). This study aims to understand and quantify this hallucination phenomenon in music-specific contexts.
AI.method: The researchers formulated hallucination as a hierarchical perceptual grounding failure across five layers (sound events, temporal properties, tonal attributes, style, and emotion). They introduced MuseDiag, a multi-paradigm diagnostic framework with contradiction-based verification. Nine models were evaluated (four open-source and five closed-source). Two training-free mitigation methods were tested: Audio-Dependency-Aware Decoding for Music (ADD-M) and Taxonomy-Guided Perceptual Anchoring (TPA).
AI.result: Three key findings: (1) Vocal misperception is a universal weakness across all nine models, tonal perception is a major axis of architectural differentiation, and Audio-Flamingo-3 remains the stable leader while substantial reordering below it reveals paradigm-specific vulnerability profiles; (2) Affirmative bias, generation-mode effects, and layer-specific perceptual limitations are empirically associated with observed hallucination patterns; (3) The two mitigation methods can reduce hallucination in probing tasks, but gains vary by model and often do not transfer to free-form generation.
AI.conclusion: Music hallucination in audio-language models requires evaluation across multiple paradigms, as mitigation methods that work in probing scenarios may not generalize to free-form generation. The study highlights the need for paradigm-specific approaches to reduce hallucination, with vocal perception and tonal attributes being critical areas for improvement.

title: Do AI Agents Understand Computer Architecture?
summary: Agents are increasingly asked to design hardware, and increasingly reported to succeed. Such reports establish that a design improved; they cannot establish why. An agent that improves an accelerator may be reasoning about the machine, or may be searching competently over knobs whose meaning it never recovers -- and only the first transfers to the next architecture. Existing evaluations cannot tell the two apart, because they vary the agent while holding the framing of the problem fixed. We do the opposite. AutoTuring hands the same agent the same 15-dimensional accelerator space twice: once as named architectural knobs with simulator counters, once as anonymous variables on [0,1], with the evaluator, the legal space and the reachable optima held identical, so that the only thing that varies is whether the problem means anything. The gap between the two is the measurement. On a nine-kernel FP16 GEMM basket, meaning pays: the architect beats a modeled H200 by 5.4% and its blind counterpart by 12.3% on average, with 70.1% fewer simulator calls. It does not pay uniquely: a critic loop recovers most of that gap for the blind agent and buys the architect nothing, so architectural knowledge and structured critique behave as substitutes rather than as complements. We report these as preliminary findings -- five to six runs per condition on a single modeled accelerator -- and take the comparison itself, not the accelerator, to be the contribution.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses a critical gap in AI hardware design research: when agents improve accelerator designs, we don't know if they understand the architecture or are just doing blind search. The authors propose a novel comparison method (AutoTuning) where the same agent tackles the same design space - once with meaningful architectural knobs and once with anonymous variables - to isolate the value of "meaning" in the problem framing.
AI.motivation: Current evaluations show agents can improve hardware designs but cannot determine whether the agent reasons about the machine or merely searches over knobs without understanding. This distinction matters because only understanding transfers to new architectures. Existing evaluations vary the agent while holding the problem framing fixed, so they cannot distinguish between these two cases.
AI.method: The authors hand the same agent the same 15-dimensional accelerator space twice: (1) as named architectural knobs with simulator counters, and (2) as anonymous variables on [0,1]. They hold the evaluator, legal space, and reachable optima identical - only varying whether the problem has semantic meaning. Tested on a nine-kernel FP16 GEMM basket, they compare the "architect" (agent with meaningful knobs) against a modeled H200 and a blind agent (with anonymous variables). They also test a critic loop to see if structured critique can substitute for architectural knowledge.
AI.result: Meaning pays significant dividends: the architect beats a modeled H200 by 5.4% and its blind counterpart by 12.3% on average, with 70.1% fewer simulator calls. However, architectural knowledge and structured critique behave as substitutes rather than complements - a critic loop recovers most of the gap for the blind agent while buying the architect nothing.
AI.conclusion: The contribution is the comparison methodology itself rather than the accelerator results. The findings are preliminary (5-6 runs per condition on a single modeled accelerator) and suggest that meaning in problem framing matters, but can be partially recovered through structured critique. The authors advocate for more rigorous evaluation in AI hardware design research to distinguish true architectural reasoning from competent blind search.

title: Personalized Federated Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Privacy-Preserving Modeling of Heterogeneous Distributed Systems
summary: We present Personalized Federated Hierarchical Gaussian Processes (pFedHGP) for probabilistic regression and classification when data are distributed across heterogeneous clients. Each client's latent function decomposes into (i) a shared global component, (ii) a client-specific deviation that shares the global kernel structure, and (iii) a flexible local residual. Sparse inducing-variable approximations and federated variational inference keep raw data local while the server synchronizes only low-dimensional statistics for the shared component. Full predictive distributions support uncertainty-aware decisions. In application studies, pFedHGP attains perfect fault classification in press tonnage monitoring using 13.77% of labeled cycles and recovers geographic zones in federated air-quality modeling without centralizing station-level time series. An Instantaneous Linear Mixing Model viewpoint links the hierarchy to multi-output Gaussian processes for correlated sensors.

AI.tldr: pFedHGP is a federated learning framework for probabilistic regression and classification across heterogeneous clients. It uses a hierarchical Gaussian process model with three components: shared global, client-specific deviation, and local residual. Sparse approximations and federated variational inference keep data local while enabling uncertainty-aware predictions.
AI.motivation: Address the challenge of distributed data across heterogeneous clients in federated learning while maintaining probabilistic uncertainty quantification and handling non-IID data distributions.
AI.method: Hierarchical Gaussian process decomposition with three components: (i) shared global component, (ii) client-specific deviation sharing global kernel structure, (iii) flexible local residual. Uses sparse inducing-variable approximations and federated variational inference to keep raw data local while synchronizing only low-dimensional statistics.
AI.result: Achieved perfect fault classification in press tonnage monitoring using only 13.77% of labeled cycles, and successfully recovered geographic zones in federated air-quality modeling without centralizing station-level data.
AI.conclusion: pFedHGP effectively handles heterogeneous federated data with uncertainty quantification, demonstrating strong performance in industrial monitoring and environmental sensing applications while preserving data privacy.

title: GS-PI: An Optimization-Decoupled Appearance Decomposition Approach for Generating PBR Gaussian Assets
summary: Gaussian Splatting (GS) excels at novel-view synthesis but encodes baked-in radiance, tightly entangling illumination with geometry and preventing seamless integration into physically based rendering (PBR) pipelines. Existing inverse-rendering methods attempt to disentangle materials via joint optimization, but often suffer from competing objectives that cause severe ambiguities and residual lighting artifacts. To overcome this, we present GS-PI, a novel optimization-decoupled framework that casts PBR material generation as a geometry-conditioned diffusion process on 3D point clouds. By operating directly in the 3D domain, our method inherently guarantees multi-view consistency, sidestepping the severe pixel correspondence issues that challenge 2D diffusion approaches. We introduce a multi-scale cross-view conditioning mechanism that integrates three complementary components: a global semantic prior, source-anchored photometric cues, and an absolute spatial learned view-direction conditioning signal. This design efficiently compresses complex multi-view evidence, mitigating cross-view projection misalignment and successfully preventing specular highlights from baking into intrinsic colors. By extracting a point cloud from a pre-trained Gaussian model, predicting PBR attributes via conditional diffusion, and distilling them back through differentiable rasterisation, we yield a fully relightable PBR-GS asset. GS-PI outperforms recent inverse-rendering baselines while replacing per-scene joint illumination/BRDF optimization with a learned diffusion pass followed by a short target-driven distillation, without requiring proxy meshes.

AI.tldr: GS-PI introduces an optimization-decoupled framework that generates physically based rendering (PBR) materials from Gaussian Splatting (GS) using a geometry-conditioned diffusion process on 3D point clouds, replacing traditional joint optimization approaches with a learned diffusion model followed by target-driven distillation.
AI.motivation: Gaussian Splatting excels at novel-view synthesis but suffers from baked-in radiance that tightly entangles illumination with geometry, preventing integration into PBR pipelines. Existing inverse-rendering methods attempt to disentangle materials via joint optimization but face competing objectives, severe ambiguities, and residual lighting artifacts.
AI.method: GS-PI operates directly in the 3D domain using a multi-scale cross-view conditioning mechanism with three components: (1) global semantic prior, (2) source-anchored photometric cues, and (3) absolute spatial learned view-direction conditioning. The pipeline extracts a point cloud from a pre-trained Gaussian model, predicts PBR attributes via conditional diffusion, and distills them back through differentiable rasterization to produce a fully relightable PBR-GS asset.
AI.result: GS-PI outperforms recent inverse-rendering baselines while replacing per-scene joint illumination/BRDF optimization with a learned diffusion pass followed by a short target-driven distillation, without requiring proxy meshes.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully prevents specular highlights from baking into intrinsic colors, mitigates cross-view projection misalignment, and achieves multi-view consistency by operating in the 3D domain, demonstrating that diffusion-based PBR material generation is a viable alternative to traditional joint optimization methods.

title: AdaRepair-Mem: Adaptive Experience Orchestration for Repository-Level Program Repair
summary: Recent memory-augmented repository-level program repair methods reuse historical repair experiences to improve LLM-based issue resolution. However, our analysis reveals three limitations in existing repository-level memory retrieval. First, episodic memory is highly imbalanced across repositories, leaving low-resource repositories with little effective support. Second, more memory does not monotonically lead to higher repair success, suggesting that relevance, quality, and redundancy matter more than raw memory volume. Third, memory accumulation is phase-misaligned: repositories may contain many reproduction experiences but few patch or refinement experiences. To address these problems, we propose an adaptive experience retrieval framework for repository-level program repair. Our framework introduces coverage-aware retrieval, which falls back to cross-repository or repair-type-based memories when same-repository memory is insufficient; quality-aware selection, which ranks memories by relevance, historical utility, specificity, and redundancy; and stage-aware routing, which separates and retrieves memories for reproduction, localization, patch generation, patch refinement, and validation. Evaluated on SWE-Bench-Lite and SWE-Bench-Verified, the proposed framework improves repair performance on under-covered repositories, reduces noisy memory retrieval, and better supports failed-to-fixed patch refinement. Our results show that the key to memory-augmented repair is not simply accumulating more experiences, but retrieving the right experiences for the right repair context.
