The key insight is that separating the common level from arm contrasts and re-estimating the level fresh each batch provides substantial benefits in non-stationary environments, though this approach is not suitable when the underlying arm performance differences are themselves changing.

title: Benchmarking MLLMs via Cognitive Expected Scene Graph for Safety-Critical Visual Negation Understanding
summary: True machine intelligence requires transcending passive pixel registration to master top-down functional reasoning over absent information via visual negation understanding. However, unconstrained visual negation paradigms remain overly open-ended, and pervasive affirmation bias causes both existing Multi-Modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and evaluation metrics to fail under negative semantics. To solve these intertwined challenges systematically, we first anchor the boundaries of negation reasoning within specific cognitive goals. Specifically, by focusing on safety as a highly pragmatic and critical cognitive dimension, we define the task of \textbf{S}cene \textbf{N}egation \textbf{U}nderstanding under \textbf{S}afety Cognition (\textbf{SNUS}). Under this framework, we construct a high-fidelity negative caption dataset mapping dense assertions of localized hazards. Concurrently, we propose the Cognitive Expected Scene Graph (CESG) Score, a structure-grounded, polarity-aware evaluation metric. Extensive experiments demonstrate that while current models struggle on the task, traditional metrics completely collapse under semantic reversals. Conversely, our framework delivers a solid benchmark for SNUS, providing a rigorous foundation to advance risk-aware situational comprehension and counterfactual cognition.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SNUS (Scene Negation Understanding under Safety Cognition), a benchmark for evaluating visual negation reasoning in multi-modal large language models (MLLMs). The authors address the challenge that current models and evaluation metrics fail under negative semantics by creating a negative caption dataset and a new metric called CESG Score.
AI.motivation: Current ML LMs and evaluation metrics suffer from affirmation bias and fail to handle visual negation understanding. There is a need for a systematic framework to advance risk-aware situational comprehension and counterfactual cognition in machine vision.
AI.method: The authors (1) define the SNUS task by focusing on safety as a cognitive dimension, (2) construct a high-fidelity negative caption dataset mapping dense assertions of localized hazards, and (3) propose the Cognitive Expected Scene Graph (CESG) Score as a structure-grounded, polarity-aware evaluation metric.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that while current models struggle on the SNUS task, traditional metrics completely collapse under semantic reversals. The proposed framework provides a solid benchmark for SNUS.
AI.conclusion: The SNUS framework delivers a rigorous foundation for advancing visual negation understanding in MLLMs, with the CESG Score providing a proper evaluation metric that handles semantic reversals where traditional metrics fail.

title: Learn Your Own Thoughts: Abstract Token Curriculum
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable reasoning capabilities by utilizing chain-of-thought (CoT) as a scratchpad for intermediate stages of thinking. However, CoT techniques require explicit supervision on thinking tokens, which requires rich, task-specific data. In this work, we propose Abstract Token Curriculum (ATC), a novel curriculum learning framework that elicits effective continuous intermediate representations without direct supervision or manual scratchpad design. ATC gradually increases problem complexity through a sequence of distributions, training the model to develop internal abstract ``thoughts'' in the continuous representation space. This paper provides both theoretical and experimental evidence for the benefits of ATC and its advantages over previous methods for training continuous thoughts. Theoretically, we show that for learning parity functions with single-layer softmax attention using ATC, attention naturally focuses on the CoT tokens in the context that provide the ``easiest path'' to predicting the next token. Experimentally, we show ATC's effectiveness on graph reachability and arithmetic learning tasks.

AI.tldr: ATC (Abstract Token Curriculum) is a novel curriculum learning framework that trains LLMs to develop internal abstract "thoughts" in continuous representation space without requiring explicit supervision or manual scratchpad design, unlike traditional chain-of-thought (CoT) methods.
AI.motivation: Chain-of-thought (CoT) techniques enable LLMs to achieve remarkable reasoning by using intermediate thinking tokens, but they require explicit supervision on thinking tokens and rich, task-specific data. This work aims to elicit effective continuous intermediate representations without direct supervision or manual scratchpad design.
AI.method: ATC uses curriculum learning by gradually increasing problem complexity through a sequence of distributions, training the model to develop internal abstract "thoughts" in the continuous representation space. Theoretically, for learning parity functions with single-layer softmax attention using ATC, attention naturally focuses on the CoT tokens in the context that provide the "easiest path" to predicting the next token.
AI.result: Theoretically, ATC enables attention to naturally focus on CoT tokens that provide the easiest path to predicting the next token when learning parity functions with single-layer softmax attention. Experimentally, ATC demonstrates effectiveness on graph reachability and arithmetic learning tasks.
AI.conclusion: ATC provides a promising approach for training continuous thoughts in LLMs without explicit supervision, with both theoretical and experimental evidence supporting its benefits over previous methods for training continuous thoughts.

title: AI Smart Glasses for Wearable Intelligence: From Egocentric Sensing to Agentic Personalization
summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping smart glasses from egocentric capture and display devices into platforms for wearable intelligence. Smart glasses increasingly serve as wearable AI systems that connect first-person observation with real-time assistance under strict form-factor constraints. We frame this transition through the lens of \emph{AI smart glasses} and define them as a system-level concept in which egocentric sensing, resource-aware computing, intelligent reasoning, multimodal interaction, and real-world application constraints are co-designed for personalized assistance in the physical world. To systematically study this perspective, we organize the survey around four connected dimensions. First, we examine the hardware foundation that bounds sensing, computation, feedback delivery, and sustained deployment. Second, we study wearable intelligence, where egocentric signals are transformed into perceptual, contextual, and agentic capabilities. Third, we discuss interaction design, through which users request, receive, correct, and regulate assistance during ongoing activity. Fourth, we analyze application scenarios across healthcare, accessibility, situated learning, daily life assistance, cultural tourism, and industrial support, showing how domain requirements reshape system design and evaluation. We further identify five cross-cutting research challenges for future AI smart glasses: next-generation hardware, trustworthy egocentric intelligence, lifelong personalized memory, proactive intelligence, and embodied foundation models. By centering smart glasses as wearable-intelligence platforms, this survey provides a unified framework for organizing technologies, applications, and open challenges in this emerging area.

AI.tldr: This survey examines AI smart glasses as wearable intelligence platforms that combine egocentric sensing, resource-aware computing, intelligent reasoning, and multimodal interaction for personalized assistance. The paper organizes research around four dimensions: hardware foundation, wearable intelligence capabilities, interaction design, and application scenarios across healthcare, accessibility, learning, and industry. Five future research challenges are identified.
AI.motivation: The transition of smart glasses from simple egocentric capture devices to comprehensive wearable AI systems requires a unified framework to organize the diverse technologies, applications, and research challenges. Existing literature lacks a systematic perspective that treats smart glasses as system-level platforms for wearable intelligence.
AI.method: This is a survey paper that organizes the analysis around four connected dimensions: (1) hardware foundation covering sensing, computation, feedback delivery, and deployment constraints; (2) wearable intelligence transforming egocentric signals into perceptual, contextual, and agentic capabilities; (3) interaction design for user request, receipt, correction, and regulation of assistance; and (4) application scenarios across healthcare, accessibility, situated learning, daily life, cultural tourism, and industrial support.
AI.result: The survey provides a unified framework organizing technologies, applications, and open challenges in AI smart glasses. It identifies five cross-cutting research challenges: next-generation hardware, trustworthy egocentric intelligence, lifelong personalized memory, proactive intelligence, and embodied foundation models.
AI.conclusion: By framing smart glasses as wearable-intelligence platforms rather than simple display devices, this survey establishes a systematic perspective for understanding and advancing this emerging field. The four-dimension framework and identified research challenges provide guidance for future research and development in AI smart glasses.

title: LearnActCoder: Role-Aware Error Memory for Adaptive Clinical Coding Agents
summary: Clinical coding agents repeatedly encounter the same failure modes, including unsupported codes, missed documented conditions, specificity errors, and procedure-coding convention mismatches. We introduce Learn-Then-Act, an inference-time adaptation framework that converts errors from a small labeled LEARN batch into a structured Mistake Knowledge Database (MistakeKDB). False-negative lessons are routed to a recall-oriented Coder, while false-positive lessons are routed to a precision-oriented Judge. We instantiate the framework in LearnActCoder, a Coder-Judge clinical coding pipeline with lookup-table grounding where available. On 150 matched MIMIC-III notes, structured MistakeKDB improves CPT F1 by 5.9 percentage points, while raw-example and reflection-style memories remain near the no-memory baseline; the ICD-9 improvement is not significant. On a matched MIMIC-IV cohort, memory shifts ICD-10 coding toward higher precision at a recall cost, leaving F1 statistically unchanged. Applying the same memory to 1,000 held-out MIMIC-III notes maintains a stable ICD operating point, providing scale/stability evidence. Overall, the results are consistent with structured, feedback-derived error memory being useful for adapting clinical coding behavior across cases without weight updates or changes to the underlying workflow. Absolute CPT/HCPCS performance remains low, and the system is evaluated retrospectively rather than in clinical deployment.

AI.tldr: Learn-Then-Act is an inference-time adaptation framework for clinical coding that converts errors from a small labeled batch into a structured Mistake Knowledge Database (MistakeKDB), routing false-negative lessons to a recall-oriented Coder and false-positive lessons to a precision-oriented Judge. The framework improves CPT F1 by 5.9 percentage points on MIMIC-III data while maintaining stable performance across scales.
AI.motivation: Clinical coding agents repeatedly encounter failure modes including unsupported codes, missed documented conditions, specificity errors, and procedure-coding convention mismatches. Existing methods for addressing these issues typically require weight updates or changes to the underlying workflow, making real-time adaptation challenging.
AI.method: The framework instantiates LearnActCoder, a Coder-Judge clinical coding pipeline with lookup-table grounding. It converts errors from a small labeled LEARN batch into a structured MistakeKDB. False-negative lessons are routed to a recall-oriented Coder, while false-positive lessons are routed to a precision-oriented Judge. The system was evaluated on matched MIMIC-III notes (150 and 1,000 notes) and a MIMIC-IV cohort.
AI.result: On 150 matched MIMIC-III notes, structured MistakeKDB improves CPT F1 by 5.9 percentage points, while raw-example and reflection-style memories remain near the no-memory baseline; ICD-9 improvement is not significant. On a matched MIMIC-IV cohort, memory shifts ICD-10 coding toward higher precision at a recall cost, leaving F1 statistically unchanged. Applying the same memory to 1,000 held-out MIMIC-III notes maintains a stable ICD operating point.
AI.conclusion: Structured, feedback-derived error memory is useful for adapting clinical coding behavior across cases without weight updates or changes to the underlying workflow. However, absolute CPT/HCPCS performance remains low, and the system is evaluated retrospectively rather than in clinical deployment.

title: Alliance Beats Isolation: Unifying Heterogeneous Allied Datasets Improves Classifier Performance
summary: In many application domains, such as student dropout, insurance fraud, loan approval, and machine failures, several labelled public datasets are available where (i) data is about the same type of objects but the set of actual underlying objects are disjoint; and (ii) the class labels are same; and (iii) the feature spaces of the datasets are largely distinct (heterogeneous), with a few shared features. We call such datasets as allied. A single classifier cannot be trained on both datasets together, and one classifier trained on one dataset cannot be tested on the other. In this paper, we propose a method to merge the feature-spaces into a single feature-space for a pair of given allied heterogeneous datasets. We then use a matrix completion method to create a unified dataset based on the merged feature-space. The hypothesis is that the merged representation facilitates the transfer of classification knowledge from one dataset to another. We conduct experiments on several pairs of allied, heterogeneous datasets and several classifiers to demonstrate that any classifier trained on the unified representation always outperforms classifiers separately trained on the constituent allied datasets on several pairs of allied datasets. This work provides an easy way to substantially improve classifier performance by unifying and using multiple allied datasets together.

title: Absence is Presence: Understanding Visual Scene Negative Events Under Safety Cognitive Constraint
summary: Traditional scene understanding focuses on affirmative information objectively present in images. However, in safety-critical domains, comprehending key information that should exist but is actually absent is vital for risk mitigation. To bridge this gap, we focus on visual scene negative captioning with safety as the cognitive constraint. The core challenge is to convert physical absence into semantic negative events. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with this process because affirmation bias suppresses negative reasoning, while limited mental filling capability and representation bias further hinder the inference of absent information. To address these challenges, we propose a negative captioning framework based on counterfactual reconstruction and contrastive decoding (CRCD). Inspired by human cognition, CRCD reformulates the task as counterfactual latent change captioning to bypass affirmation bias. It contrasts a synthesized safe expectation with reality to identify semantic omissions. To address limited mental filling, we design a dual-branch counterfactual reconstruction architecture. The amodal completion branch restores defective objects, while the functional association branch infers completely absent safety objects. Concurrently, a multi-condition representation learning mechanism is integrated to mitigate representation bias by projecting universal features onto predefined safety criteria subspaces, thereby capturing information across more dimensions. By decoding feature-level semantic residuals between the reconstructed scene prototype and raw input, CRCD bounds the non-existence search space and activates the decoder's negative logic. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of CRCD, establishing a high-performance baseline for this pioneering task.

title: AutoData: Agentic Search for Pre-training Data Selection
summary: LLM agents have recently shown promise in automating machine learning engineering by editing model and training code under execution feedback. Data, however, remains largely outside this agentic optimisation loop. We frame pre-training data selection as heuristic engineering over per-document features, i.e., lexical statistics, categorical labels, and perplexity. We introduce AutoData, an agent that searches directly over executable selection algorithms. Unlike prior data mixture methods that optimise weights over a fixed set of domains, AutoData searches a richer program space of scoring, stratification, and stochastic selection rules, discovering feature interactions automatically by iteratively refining algorithms with validation feedback from a proxy model. Within an overnight search, AutoData discovers a selection algorithm that outperforms existing human-designed curation pipelines. Despite being searched only on this small proxy, the discovered recipe transfers to larger scales and improves the downstream metric CORE. These results suggest that data engineering can be treated as an agentic machine learning problem, extending autonomous research from model and training-code optimization to the data.

AI.tldr: AutoData is an LLM agent that autonomously searches for pre-training data selection algorithms, outperforming human-designed curation pipelines and transferring effectively to larger scales.
AI.motivation: LLM agents have automated model and training code optimization but data remains largely outside this agentic loop. This work aims to treat data engineering as an agentic ML problem.
AI.method: Framed pre-training data selection as heuristic engineering over per-document features (lexical statistics, categorical labels, perplexity). AutoData searches a program space of scoring, stratification, and stochastic selection rules, iteratively refining algorithms using validation feedback from a proxy model.
AI.result: Within an overnight search, AutoData discovered a selection algorithm outperforming existing human-designed curation pipelines. The discovered recipe transfers to larger scales and improves downstream metric CORE.
AI.conclusion: Data engineering can be treated as an agentic machine learning problem, extending autonomous research from model and training-code optimization to the data domain.

title: OceanMoE: Structured Conditional Sparse Computation for Long-Horizon Multivariate Ocean Forecasting
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Yishun Zhu and Jian Wang contributed equally to this research
summary: Multivariate ocean forecasting must exploit shared evolution in a coupled ocean system while adapting to the heterogeneous statistical and dynamical characteristics of different prediction variables and locations. Fully shared models may lack the flexibility to handle this heterogeneity, whereas fully independent models discard the common ocean context shared across variables. The key question is how to retain shared context in a unified model while allowing computation to specialize according to the prediction target and local state. We propose OceanMoE, a structured conditional sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework that combines sharing and specialization for multivariate ocean forecasting. OceanMoE fuses cross-variable information to construct target-specific local representations and uses them to perform content-conditioned sparse routing at each spatial location, with the number of active experts adapted to router confidence. In the decoder, routing is augmented with a learned geographic bias parameterized by spherical-harmonic spatial bases, while shared residual and seasonal pathways provide common cross-variable and month-dependent context. Experiments on long-horizon autoregressive ORAS5 forecasting show that OceanMoE lowers aggregate forecasting error in both evaluated settings and maintains lower geometric-mean normalized RMSE than the corresponding baselines over most later rollout months. Routing analyses further show that expert allocation varies with prediction targets and spatial locations. These results support structured conditional computation as a modeling strategy for balancing shared ocean context with adaptive specialization.

AI.tldr: OceanMoE is a structured conditional sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework designed for multivariate ocean forecasting. It balances shared ocean context with adaptive specialization by using content-conditioned sparse routing that adapts the number of active experts based on router confidence, augmented with geographic bias using spherical-harmonic spatial bases.
AI.motivation: Multivariate ocean forecasting requires exploiting shared evolution in coupled ocean systems while adapting to heterogeneous statistical and dynamical characteristics of different prediction variables and locations. Existing fully shared models lack flexibility, while fully independent models discard common ocean context. The core challenge is retaining shared context in a unified model while allowing computation to specialize per prediction target and local state.
AI.method: OceanMoE combines sharing and specialization through: (1) Cross-variable information fusion to construct target-specific local representations; (2) Content-conditioned sparse routing at each spatial location with expert count adapted to router confidence; (3) Learned geographic bias using spherical-harmonic spatial bases in the decoder; (4) Shared residual and seasonal pathways providing common cross-variable and month-dependent context.
AI.result: On long-horizon autoregressive ORAS5 forecasting: OceanMoE lowers aggregate forecasting error in both evaluated settings and maintains lower geometric-mean normalized RMSE than baselines over most later rollout months. Expert allocation varies with prediction targets and spatial locations.
AI.conclusion: Structured conditional computation is a viable modeling strategy for balancing shared ocean context with adaptive specialization in multivariate ocean forecasting. The method successfully handles heterogeneity across variables and locations while preserving common ocean dynamics.

title: SnapPhysics: A Physics-Aware Scene Graph from a Single View for Interactive Mixed Reality Scenes
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE ISMAR, 2026
summary: We propose SnapPhysics, a training-free framework that reconstructs 3D objects and estimates their physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of gravity from a single image. For physically coherent interactions in mixed reality (MR), such properties are as important as geometry. Prior approaches infer them by analyzing object dynamics in video, which is computationally costly, or by querying vision-language models (VLMs) on single images, which lacks geometric grounding and inter-object relationships. We address these limitations by combining instance-level 3D reconstruction and spatial alignment with a physics-aware scene graph that encodes these relationships and per-object metric geometry as structured context for VLM-based property reasoning. Experiments on 3D-FRONT show that SnapPhysics improves scene-level F-Score by 18.6% over the best learning-based method, and on real captured scenes with ground-truth mass, it reduces the mean absolute log difference error (mALDE) by up to 20.5% and improves log-scale correlation ($r^2_{\mathrm{ls}}$) by up to 19.6% over VLM-only estimation. SnapPhysics enables physically interactive MR experiences without manual parameter tuning. Project page: https://snapphysics-ismar2026.github.io/.

AI.tldr: SnapPhysics is a training-free framework that reconstructs 3D objects and estimates physical properties (mass, friction, center of gravity) from a single image for mixed reality applications. It combines instance-level 3D reconstruction with a physics-aware scene graph that provides structured context for VLM-based property reasoning.
AI.motivation: Physical properties (mass, friction, center of gravity) are as important as geometry for physically coherent interactions in mixed reality (MR). Prior approaches either require costly video analysis to infer properties from object dynamics, or use vision-language models (VLMs) on single images which lack geometric grounding and inter-object relationships.
AI.method: The framework combines instance-level 3D reconstruction and spatial alignment with a physics-aware scene graph. This scene graph encodes inter-object relationships and per-object metric geometry as structured context for VLM-based property reasoning. The approach is training-free.
AI.result: On 3D-FRONT dataset, SnapPhysics improves scene-level F-Score by 18.6% over the best learning-based method. On real captured scenes with ground-truth mass, it reduces mean absolute log difference error (mALDE) by up to 20.5% and improves log-scale correlation (r²_ls) by up to 19.6% compared to VLM-only estimation.
AI.conclusion: SnapPhysics enables physically interactive MR experiences without manual parameter tuning by accurately estimating physical properties from single images through the integration of 3D reconstruction and VLM-based reasoning.

title: Rethinking Multi-Agent Collaboration: When More Is Less
summary: The rapid advancement of large language models and single-agent harnesses has reshaped the landscape of autonomous systems, raising a critical question of when multi-agent collaboration offers genuine value. As individual agent capabilities continue to scale, multi-agent collaboration faces diminishing returns while incurring growing context overhead. Through systematic analysis, we delineate the capability boundaries of multi-agent collaboration relative to single-agent alternatives, showing that it confers systematic benefits specifically in long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies, while single-agent harnesses remain superior in tightly coupled, sequential workflows. Building on these insights, we propose SAIGE, a lightweight multi-agent collaboration mechanism based on Semantic-Aware Incremental Graph Evolution. SAIGE models collaboration as a dynamically evolving graph, where nodes are agent instances spawned on demand and edges encode semantic dependencies established through content-based information retrieval. Experiments on long-horizon, complex task benchmarks show that SAIGE achieves a favorable trade-off between context efficiency and task performance, and that scaling the agent pool or deepening the recursion level does not consistently improve outcomes. Our findings suggest that multi-agent superiority is bounded by task structure rather than universal, and that more agents do not necessarily make a system more intelligent.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates when multi-agent collaboration provides genuine value over single-agent systems in LLM-based autonomous systems, proposing SAIGE - a lightweight multi-agent mechanism using Semantic-Aware Incremental Graph Evolution that models collaboration as dynamically evolving graphs with content-based semantic dependencies.
AI.motivation: The rapid advancement of LLMs and single-agent systems raises a critical question: when does multi-agent collaboration actually offer value? As individual agent capabilities scale, multi-agent approaches face diminishing returns while incurring growing context overhead, making it essential to understand their capability boundaries.
AI.method: The researchers conducted systematic analysis to delineate the capability boundaries of multi-agent collaboration relative to single-agent alternatives, then developed SAIGE which models collaboration as a dynamically evolving graph where nodes are agent instances spawned on demand and edges encode semantic dependencies through content-based information retrieval. Experiments were conducted on long-horizon, complex task benchmarks.
AI.result: Multi-agent collaboration provides systematic benefits specifically in long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies, while single-agent harnesses remain superior in tightly coupled, sequential workflows. SAIGE achieves a favorable trade-off between context efficiency and task performance. Critically, scaling the agent pool or deepening recursion levels does not consistently improve outcomes.
AI.conclusion: Multi-agent superiority is bounded by task structure rather than universal - more agents do not necessarily make a system more intelligent. The value of multi-agent collaboration depends on the specific task characteristics, not the number or complexity of agents deployed.

title: PhyRestore: Physics-Structured Latent-Factor Restoration
summary: Estimating temporal soil-loss change is challenging when physically meaningful input factors are noisy or corrupted, particularly because substantial changes are rare relative to the large number of locations exhibiting little change. We study this problem through the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) and introduce PhyRestore, a physics-structured latent-factor restoration framework. Rather than directly predicting soil-loss change or correcting a degraded physical estimate, PhyRestore restores corrupted physical factors and reconstructs temporal change through the known physical relationship. We evaluate PhyRestore in a watershed-scale bitemporal raster setting under isolated and simultaneous corruption of rainfall erosivity and cover management, comparing it with the degraded RUSLE estimate and Direct RF, XGBoost, MLP, and CNN models. Factor restoration improves high-magnitude recovery when the corrupted factors remain identifiable, but its advantage weakens under joint corruption, sparse positive extremes, and factor values outside the training support.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces PhyRestore, a physics-structured latent-factor restoration framework for estimating temporal soil-loss change using RUSLE. It addresses the challenge of noisy or corrupted physical input factors by restoring corrupted factors through known physical relationships rather than directly predicting soil-loss change.
AI.motivation: The core challenge is that estimating temporal soil-loss change is difficult when physically meaningful input factors are noisy or corrupted, particularly because substantial changes are rare relative to locations showing little change. Traditional methods struggle with this imbalance and data quality issues.
AI.method: PhyRestore restores corrupted physical factors and reconstructs temporal change through the known physical relationship (RUSLE). The framework is evaluated in a watershed-scale bitemporal raster setting under isolated and simultaneous corruption of rainfall erosivity and cover management factors. Performance is compared against degraded RUSLE estimates and machine learning models including Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP, and CNN.
AI.result: Factor restoration improves high-magnitude recovery when corrupted factors remain identifiable. However, the advantage weakens under joint corruption, sparse positive extremes, and factor values outside the training support.
AI.conclusion: The physics-structured approach of PhyRestore shows promise for improving soil-loss change estimation, but its effectiveness is limited by factors such as joint corruption of multiple input variables, sparse extreme values, and extrapolation beyond training data distribution.

title: KoUniTalk: A Lightweight Articulation-Centered Korean-English 3D Talking Face Benchmark
summary: High-quality 3D talking face datasets remain largely English- centric, and Korean 3D facial motion data are difficult to combine with standard English benchmarks because of differences in mesh topology, spatial scale, coordinate system, and temporal sampling. We present KoUniTalk, a lightweight articulation-centered Korean-English 3D talk- ing face benchmark that retargets VOCASET and the released Korean speech-based 3D talking face data to a shared mesh topology using de- formation transfer. Rather than proposing a new deformation-transfer algorithm or a full-head identity-preserving avatar dataset, KoUniTalk provides an identity-neutral canonical output space for controlled speech- driven facial articulation training and evaluation across English and Ko- rean. The unified template contains 1,176 vertices and focuses on the mouth and adjacent lower- and mid-face regions, reducing the output dimensionality from 15,069 and 72,147 dimensions to 3,528 dimensions, corresponding to 4.27-fold and 20.45-fold reductions compared with VO- CASET/FLAME and the original Korean mesh, respectively. To exam- ine whether retargeting preserves speech-relevant motion, we evaluate semantic mouth-landmark trajectories, including mouth opening, mouth width, aperture ratio, and mouth-opening dynamics. Since the official test set of the Korean dataset is not publicly released, we additionally define a subject-disjoint Korean benchmark split. The processed matched benchmark contains 22 speakers, 4,978 sequences, and 642,781 frames, enabling Korean-English cross-dataset evaluation of speech-driven 3D fa- cial animation models in a single compact articulation-template space. Source-reported inventory counts are listed separately from these pro- cessed counts

AI.tldr: KoUniTalk is a Korean-English 3D talking face benchmark that retargets VOCASET and Korean speech-based 3D facial data to a unified mesh topology using deformation transfer. The unified template contains 1,176 vertices focusing on mouth and adjacent facial regions, reducing output dimensionality by 4.27-fold (VOCASET/FLAME) and 20.45-fold (original Korean mesh). The benchmark contains 22 speakers, 4,978 sequences, and 642,781 frames for cross-dataset evaluation.
AI.motivation: High-quality 3D talking face datasets are largely English-centric, and Korean 3D facial motion data cannot be combined with standard English benchmarks due to differences in mesh topology, spatial scale, coordinate system, and temporal sampling. There is a need for a unified benchmark enabling Korean-English cross-dataset evaluation.
AI.method: The paper uses deformation transfer to retarget VOCASET and Korean 3D talking face data to a shared mesh topology, creating an identity-neutral canonical output space. The unified template contains 1,176 vertices focusing on mouth and adjacent lower- and mid-face regions. Semantic mouth-landmark trajectories (mouth opening, mouth width, aperture ratio, mouth-opening dynamics) are evaluated to verify preservation of speech-relevant motion. A subject-disjoint Korean benchmark split is defined since the official test set is not publicly released.
AI.result: The processed benchmark contains 22 speakers, 4,978 sequences, and 642,781 frames. Dimensionality reduced from 15,069 (VOCASET/FLAME) and 72,147 (original Korean mesh) to 3,528 dimensions (4.27-fold and 20.45-fold reductions respectively). The retargeting preserves speech-relevant motion as verified by semantic mouth-landmark trajectory analysis.
AI.conclusion: KoUniTalk provides a unified, compact articulation-template space enabling Korean-English cross-dataset evaluation of speech-driven 3D facial animation models. It addresses the lack of Korean 3D talking face benchmarks compatible with English datasets.

title: TorchCraft: Unified binder design by inverting an all-atom structure predictor
summary: All-atom structure predictors model diverse molecular interactions, but using their learned structural priors for binder design remains challenging. Here we present TorchCraft, a unified binder-design framework that optimizes sequence logits through a frozen all-atom predictor. Implemented in TorchFold, TorchCraft combines confidence, contact, geometric, and sequence-prior objectives within a shared optimization procedure for minibinders, framework-conditioned VHHs, cyclic peptides, and ligand-binding proteins. Using pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights, TorchCraft generated representative minibinders and VHHs with experimentally measured binding across four targets in each format, without post hoc sequence redesign. Computational benchmarks further demonstrated the framework's applicability to cyclic peptides and ligand-conditioned pocket design. TorchCraft extends predictor inversion to multiple binder formats and molecular contexts, providing a common framework for reusing all-atom structural priors in design.

AI.tldr: TorchCraft is a unified binder-design framework that optimizes sequence logits through a frozen all-atom predictor (AlphaFold 3), combining multiple objectives (confidence, contact, geometric, sequence-prior) to design minibinders, VHHs, cyclic peptides, and ligand-binding proteins without post hoc sequence redesign.
AI.motivation: All-atom structure predictors can model diverse molecular interactions, but using their learned structural priors for binder design remains challenging. There was a need for a unified framework to leverage these predictors for designing various binder formats.
AI.method: TorchCraft uses pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights and optimizes sequence logits through the frozen predictor. It combines confidence, contact, geometric, and sequence-prior objectives within a shared optimization procedure implemented in TorchFold. This allows inversion of the predictor for binder design across multiple formats.
AI.result: TorchCraft generated representative minibinders and VHHs with experimentally measured binding across four targets in each format. The framework was also demonstrated on cyclic peptides and ligand-conditioned pocket design through computational benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: TorchCraft extends predictor inversion to multiple binder formats and molecular contexts, providing a common framework for reusing all-atom structural priors in protein design. It successfully designs binders without requiring post hoc sequence redesign.

title: Learning-Based Reconstruction of Optical Properties in Bilayered Media from Single-distance Time-Resolved Reflectance Measurements
summary: The inverse problem of reconstructing optical properties, specifically absorption and scattering coefficients, in layered biological media from time-domain reflectance measurements remains a significant challenge for traditional analytical models. Inverse solvers based on the diffusion equation often struggle with structural heterogeneity, frequently yielding poor accuracy for superficial absorption and deep-layers scattering. In this work, we propose a machine learning framework as an alternative approach to reconstruct the optical properties of a bilayered medium, benchmarking its efficiency and accuracy against model-based algorithms. To overcome the intrinsic approximations of diffusion theory and inverse reconstruction, we generated a robust synthetic dataset of forward DTOF using exact Monte Carlo simulations at multiple source-detector distances. A machine learning pipeline was then trained on this dataset and validated against state-of-the-art model-based reconstruction methods. Besides the significant reconstruction speed-up, the machine learning approach achieves higher accuracy than model-based inverse solvers, further providing an estimate of the parameter space dimensionality without requiring any a priori information about the number of layers in the investigated geometry. Further enhancements in the reconstruction accuracy can be expected in future extensions of this work, by training the pipeline over multiple DTOF curves from the same medium, in a joint multi-distance reconstruction approach.

AI.tldr: A machine learning framework is proposed to reconstruct optical properties (absorption and scattering coefficients) in bilayered biological media from time-domain reflectance measurements, outperforming traditional model-based inverse solvers in accuracy and speed while also estimating parameter space dimensionality without prior layer information.
AI.motivation: Traditional diffusion equation-based inverse solvers struggle with structural heterogeneity in layered biological media, yielding poor accuracy for superficial absorption and deep-layer scattering. There is a need for more accurate and efficient reconstruction methods.
AI.method: A machine learning pipeline was trained on a synthetic dataset generated from exact Monte Carlo simulations of forward diffuse time-of-flight (DTOF) measurements at multiple source-detector distances. The approach was validated against state-of-the-art model-based reconstruction methods.
AI.result: The machine learning approach achieves higher accuracy than model-based inverse solvers with significant reconstruction speed-up. It also provides an estimate of parameter space dimensionality without requiring a priori information about the number of layers.
AI.conclusion: The ML framework demonstrates superior performance for optical property reconstruction in layered media. Future work will focus on multi-distance reconstruction by training over multiple DTOF curves from the same medium to further enhance accuracy.

title: PACE: Precise AI Cinematic Expression: A Typed Specification for Script-Grounded Previsualization and Geometric Conformance
summary:
Between a screenplay and a film sits a planning problem that is spatial first: who stands where, and what a camera sees from where it stands. An image diffusion model asked for a shot in free text settles that plan by its own defaults. We present PACE (Precise AI Cinematic Expression), a typed representation for the plan: the screenplay evidence, the characters, props and locations it needs, where each subject stands, and what the camera does. A value is written once at the level it belongs to (script, scene, shot or panel) and inherited below it. A compiler turns the result into both the prompt sent to the diffusion model and a 3D scene built in metres, and a camera solver places the camera so that the declared framing is the framing built. Where a declared value becomes geometry, PACE measures, field by field, how far the compiled camera and the staged render sit from the declaration, rather than asking a model to judge.
  On the 11-scene Automatic Drive screenplay, every staged single-subject panel places its subject within 1.2% of frame width of its declared position; with two or three subjects one camera pose cannot satisfy every position, and the residual is reported rather than absorbed. On 204 external director-storyboard shots, delivered head height is 1.906 times the staged target from the director's words, 1.733 from the compiled prompt, and 0.955 with the greybox control; the condition that holds framing best draws the described action least. Declaring the pose on 30 shots raises the action drawn from 58.9% to 74.4% without moving the framing. Transitions, fitted motion and human review of the generated panels remain open. Code: https://github.com/StudioPiLabs/pace-core

AI.tldr: PACE (Precise AI Cinematic Expression) is a typed representation system that bridges screenplays and AI-generated film by encoding spatial planning (character positions, camera placement) as structured data that can be compiled into both diffusion model prompts and 3D scenes, with built-in measurement of discrepancies between declared and actual framing.
AI.motivation: The gap between screenplay and film involves a spatial planning problem (who stands where, what camera sees) that current image diffusion models settle by their own defaults, lacking precise control over cinematic composition.
AI.method: PACE uses a hierarchical typed representation where values are written at one level (script/scene/shot/panel) and inherited below. A compiler converts PACE specifications into both text prompts for diffusion models and 3D scenes with metric coordinates. A camera solver places cameras to achieve declared framing. Error is measured field-by-field rather than relying on model judgment.
AI.result: Single-subject panels achieve 1.2% frame width accuracy. With 2-3 subjects, conflicts are reported rather than absorbed. External director-storyboard shots show head height delivery of 1.906x (director's words), 1.733x (compiled prompt), 0.955x (greybox control). Declaring pose on 30 shots improved action drawing from 58.9% to 74.4% without affecting framing.
AI.conclusion: PACE provides precise control over AI-generated cinematic composition through declarative specifications, though trade-offs exist between framing accuracy and action fidelity. Open problems include transitions, fitted motion, and human review of generated panels.

title: Integrating knowledge from case reports: a medical ontology based multimodal information system with structured summary
summary: Published medical case reports serve as a crucial medical information carrier, documenting discoveries in rare diseases, diagnostic methods, and innovative treatments. Despite the wealth of clinical knowledge in millions of case reports in the public medicine literature database (PubMed), accessing relevant information efficiently is hindered by the limitations of traditional keyword-based retrieval tools on unstructured and diverse case reports. To address the above issues, we introduce a comprehensive multimodal information system for case reports integrating structured clinical summaries of patients including medical images and biomedical named entities from 52949 open-access case reports published from 2000 to 2021. The multimodal essential information is organized in a well-structured medical ontology. Also, a powerful interface for searching and browsing case reports is designed to assist junior clinicians in retrieving cases effectively and improving the identification and diagnosis of rare diseases.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multimodal information system for medical case reports that integrates structured clinical summaries, medical images, and biomedical named entities from 52,949 open-access case reports (2000-2021), organized via a medical ontology to facilitate efficient retrieval for clinicians.
AI.motivation: Published medical case reports contain valuable clinical knowledge about rare diseases, diagnostic methods, and innovative treatments, but traditional keyword-based retrieval tools are inadequate for efficiently accessing this wealth of information due to the unstructured and diverse nature of case reports.
AI.method: The researchers developed a comprehensive multimodal information system that: (1) extracted structured clinical summaries including patient information, (2) incorporated medical images, (3) identified biomedical named entities, (4) organized all this multimodal data using a well-structured medical ontology, and (5) designed a powerful search and browsing interface. The system was built using 52,949 open-access case reports published from 2000 to 2021.
AI.result: A comprehensive multimodal information system integrating structured clinical summaries, medical images, and biomedical named entities from 52,949 case reports, organized through a medical ontology with an effective search interface.
AI.conclusion: The developed system assists junior clinicians in retrieving relevant cases effectively and improves the identification and diagnosis of rare diseases by providing structured, multimodal access to the vast repository of medical case report literature.

title: DeliveryGym: An RL Environment for Long-Horizon Embodied Agent Planning with Adaptive Curriculum
summary: Executable environments enable LLM agents to learn from the consequences of their actions. For embodied agents, those consequences extend beyond whether the current task succeeds: completing a delivery can consume the time, energy, or money needed for later work. Learning to plan therefore requires environments that preserve these dependencies and turn them into feedback across a complete trajectory. We introduce DeliveryGym, a 3D environment for evaluating and training agents on continuous courier shifts. It couples multimodal tool interaction with persistent world dynamics and computes trajectory rewards from simulator events, making the costs of an agent's decisions available for reinforcement learning (RL). The environment also adapts future training shifts to the policy's observed weaknesses while keeping evaluation fixed. Across six models and 13 city maps, evaluation exposes a gap between reliably executing assigned deliveries and choosing and sequencing work over a shift. On the fixed test suite, RL improves Qwen3-VL-4B's net income by 54.3%, showing that learning from complete shifts improves performance under these coupled constraints. Adapting the training environment improves test income by 16.5% over uniform sampling at the same rollout budget, indicating that which situations an agent practices also matters. DeliveryGym provides an executable setting for studying how agents learn to coordinate deliveries and preserve resources for later orders within an episode.

AI.tldr: DeliveryGym is a 3D environment for training and evaluating LLM agents on continuous courier shifts, with persistent world dynamics and trajectory-based rewards. RL improves Qwen3-VL-4B's net income by 54.3%, and adaptive training provides 16.5% improvement over uniform sampling.
AI.motivation: Training LLM agents in embodied environments requires understanding that actions have consequences extending beyond immediate task success (e.g., time, energy, money consumption). Existing environments fail to preserve these dependencies across complete trajectories, making it difficult to learn planning skills.
AI.method: Introduce DeliveryGym, a 3D environment for continuous courier shifts that couples multimodal tool interaction with persistent world dynamics. The environment computes trajectory rewards from simulator events, making decision costs available for RL. It adapts future training shifts to the policy's observed weaknesses while keeping evaluation fixed. Evaluate across six models and 13 city maps.
AI.result: On fixed test suite, RL improves Qwen3-VL-4B's net income by 54.3%. Adaptive training improves test income by 16.5% over uniform sampling at same rollout budget. Evaluation exposes a gap between reliably executing deliveries and choosing/sequencing work over a shift.
AI.conclusion: Learning from complete shifts improves performance under coupled constraints. Which situations an agent practices (adaptive training) matters significantly for test performance. DeliveryGym provides an executable setting for studying how agents learn to coordinate deliveries and preserve resources within episodes.

title: Socialized UAV Cross-Task Learning: Towards Cross-Granularity Collaboration through Hierarchical Interaction
summary: Joint learning across heterogeneous tasks is often treated as task coupling through feature sharing, distillation, or auxiliary supervision. However, in cross-task learning, mismatched representational and supervisory granularities make such coupling prone to interference, teacher bias, or unidirectional collapse. We argue that cross-granularity learning is fundamentally a problem of hierarchical interaction regulation rather than simple task coupling. This issue is particularly evident in UAV perception, where visual shifts and detection--segmentation objectives naturally form coarse- and fine-grained knowledge sources. To systematically study this problem, we introduce CrossUAV, a UAV benchmark for joint object detection and instance segmentation that provides a unified evaluation platform for cross-granularity task collaboration. To address these challenges, we propose Cross-Granularity Socialized Collaboration (CGSC), a progressive and adaptive framework that regulates when, where, and how tasks exchange information across network hierarchies. CGSC progressively activates cross-task interactions and adaptively adjusts the strength according to task contribution, suppressing harmful interference while exploiting complementary coarse- and fine-grained structures. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements on both tasks, validating hierarchical dynamic interaction as an effective mechanism for cross-granularity collaboration.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses cross-granularity learning in UAV perception, where joint object detection (coarse-grained) and instance segmentation (fine-grained) suffer from interference due to mismatched representational granularities. The authors propose CrossUAV, a unified benchmark for this task, and CGSC, a framework that progressively and adaptively regulates cross-task interactions across network hierarchies to suppress harmful interference while exploiting complementary knowledge.
AI.motivation: Current cross-task learning methods treat task coupling through feature sharing, distillation, or auxiliary supervision, which lead to interference, teacher bias, or unidirectional collapse when dealing with tasks at different granularity levels (coarse vs fine). This is particularly problematic in UAV perception where visual shifts and detection-segmentation objectives naturally form heterogeneous knowledge sources.
AI.method: The proposed CGSC framework uses a progressive and adaptive mechanism that regulates: (1) WHEN to activate cross-task interactions (progressive activation), (2) WHERE to exchange information across network hierarchies, and (3) HOW to adjust interaction strength according to task contribution. This hierarchical dynamic interaction suppresses harmful interference while exploiting complementary coarse- and fine-grained structures.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements on both detection and segmentation tasks, validating hierarchical dynamic interaction as an effective mechanism for cross-granularity collaboration.
AI.conclusion: Cross-granularity learning should be viewed as a problem of hierarchical interaction regulation rather than simple task coupling. The CrossUAV benchmark provides a unified evaluation platform for studying this problem, and CGSC's progressive and adaptive interaction mechanism offers an effective solution for UAV perception tasks requiring joint detection and segmentation.

title: Contagion on the Trading Floor: How Adversarial Signals Spread in Multi-Agent Trading Systems
comment: Published in ECML PKDD 2026. 25 pages, including 7 pages of supplementary material
summary: Multi-agent trading systems built on large language models (LLMs) are beginning to appear in quantitative finance, yet their robustness to adversarial inputs is largely unknown. We study the vulnerability of LLM trading stacks to black-box, input-only attacks that enter solely via admissible social-media feeds. We introduce the Generic Multi-Agent Trading System (GMATS), a framework that captures modern multiagent trading architectures and instantiate a class of black-box poisoning attackers that treat an LLM as a post generator and inject budget-constrained, plausibly benign social-media content into the analyst's evidence stream. We define contagion metrics that trace how adversarial content propagates through the stack, including belief-shift scores at analyst and coordinator layers and attack-clean deltas on standard backtest metrics. Experiments on a safe offline benchmark with historical market and social data show that even simple input-only attackers can materially degrade risk-return profiles, sharply reducing Sharpe ratios. At the same time, we find that suitably designed multi-agent topologies and coordinator prompts can dampen adversarial shocks and improve average robustness under identical poisoning budgets.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the vulnerability of LLM-based multi-agent trading systems to adversarial inputs through social media feeds, introducing GMATS framework and demonstrating that simple poisoning attacks can significantly degrade trading performance while multi-agent topologies can enhance robustness.
AI.motivation: Multi-agent trading systems using LLMs are emerging in quantitative finance, but their robustness against adversarial attacks remains unknown. The research addresses this critical security gap by studying black-box, input-only attacks that inject malicious content into social-media feeds.
AI.method: The authors introduce GMATS framework to capture modern multi-agent trading architectures, define black-box poisoning attackers treating LLMs as post generators, establish contagion metrics (belief-shift scores, attack-clean deltas), and conduct experiments on offline benchmarks with historical market and social data.
AI.result: Even simple input-only attackers can materially degrade risk-return profiles, sharply reducing Sharpe ratios. However, suitably designed multi-agent topologies and coordinator prompts can dampen adversarial shocks and improve average robustness under identical poisoning budgets.
AI.conclusion: LLM-based multi-agent trading systems are vulnerable to adversarial social-media inputs, but architectural design choices (topologies and coordinator prompts) can significantly enhance robustness against such attacks.

title: Beyond Flattened Tokens: Structure-Preserving EEG Decoding with Reusable TriDim Blocks
summary: Effective EEG decoding requires representations that preserve organization among channels, local waveform dynamics, and long-range temporal context. Existing EEG architectures often capture these structures using separate specialized modules or collapse them into a single token sequence, making it difficult to maintain their distinct roles and coordinate their interactions throughout the backbone. We propose TriDim, a reusable block that preserves the representation shape and keeps three EEG axes explicit: channel, sample position within each patch, and patch position across the recording. These axes correspond to spatial, short-term temporal, and long-term temporal information, respectively. Each TriDim block applies feed-forward transformations along individual axes and cross-axis attention to coordinate information exchange among them. By stacking TriDim blocks with a multi-level tri-axis readout, we construct TriDimEEG, a standalone EEG decoder. Under strict cross-subject evaluation on eight datasets spanning clinical diagnosis, sleep staging, motor imagery, and emotion recognition, TriDimEEG achieves the best overall performance among fifteen evaluated models, with a 4.3% relative improvement in average accuracy over the second-best model. Replacing Transformer blocks in three EEG foundation models with TriDim blocks yields an average relative improvement of 7.4% in downstream accuracy while reducing parameter counts by 17.0% to 47.3%. These results establish TriDim as an effective and reusable building block and TriDimEEG as a strong standalone EEG decoder. Code and parameters of TriDimEEG are available at https://github.com/ncclab-sustech/TriDim_model.

AI.tldr: TriDim is a novel neural network block for EEG decoding that explicitly maintains three axes (channel/spatial, sample position/short-term temporal, patch position/long-term temporal) and uses feed-forward transformations along individual axes with cross-axis attention. TriDimEEG, built by stacking TriDim blocks, achieves state-of-the-art performance across 8 datasets and 4 tasks, with 4.3% relative improvement over the second-best model, and can replace Transformer blocks in EEG foundation models for 7.4% average improvement with significant parameter reduction.
AI.motivation: Existing EEG architectures either use separate specialized modules or collapse all information into a single token sequence, making it difficult to maintain distinct roles of spatial, short-term temporal, and long-term temporal information and coordinate their interactions throughout the backbone.
AI.method: TriDim block preserves representation shape with three explicit EEG axes: (1) channel (spatial), (2) sample position within each patch (short-term temporal), and (3) patch position across recording (long-term temporal). Each block applies feed-forward transformations along individual axes and cross-axis attention to coordinate information exchange. TriDimEEG stacks these blocks with a multi-level tri-axis readout.
AI.result: TriDimEEG achieves best overall performance among 15 evaluated models on 8 datasets spanning clinical diagnosis, sleep staging, motor imagery, and emotion recognition, with 4.3% relative improvement in average accuracy over the second-best model. When replacing Transformer blocks in three EEG foundation models, TriDim yields 7.4% average relative improvement while reducing parameters by 17.0% to 47.3%.
AI.conclusion: TriDim is an effective and reusable building block for EEG processing, and TriDimEEG serves as a strong standalone EEG decoder. The approach demonstrates that explicitly maintaining three EEG axes with specialized transformations and cross-axis attention outperforms traditional approaches.

title: Steering Equilibrium Selection in Regularized Self-Play via the Reference Policy
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Companion to arXiv:2606.28308 and arXiv:2607.17543. Fully reproducible: a single self-contained notebook regenerates every number, table, and figure
summary: Regularized self-play -- the family behind DeepNash's Stratego play -- drives a two-player zero-sum policy to a Nash equilibrium by best-responding to a slowly moving, entropy-regularized reference policy $ρ$. When the game has a polytope of value-equivalent equilibria, the regularizer silently breaks the tie: with a uniform reference it selects the maximum-entropy member, the I-projection of $ρ$ onto the Nash set. Can the reference be used to choose the equilibrium on purpose? On five exactly solvable games plus a 2-D polytope, with exact best responses and equivalence tests over independent seeds, anchoring the reference at a target member and refining steers self-play to that member with mean coordinate error 0.007 at median exploitability $5\times10^{-5}$, TOST-equivalent to the request within $\pm0.05$; the anchoring persists through refinement and follows the reference, not the initialization. Selection follows the reach-weighted I-projection (slope 0.969 [0.950, 0.987]). We report with equal emphasis where the story breaks: fixed off-manifold references cost 0.08-0.25 exploitability; stiff or flat families require a smaller mirror step, set by a pre-registered rule; boundary targets undershoot; curvature predicts where boundary saturation bites (rank correlation 0.90, p=0.037) while interior precision is curvature-independent. Table and MLP steering maps are equivalent within $\pm0.03$ at every target (30 seeds); matched control arms show attention's robust signature is excess seed variance, any systematic shift bounded at 0.018 and not significant. Against a best response the selection-robustness trade-off is degenerate: steering matters only against fixed, non-equilibrium opponents. The recipe -- anchor the reference at the desired member and refine -- reinterprets the KL anchor of RLHF-style RL as a selection knob, not only a stability leash.

AI.tldr: This paper explores using a reference policy in regularized self-play to deliberately select specific Nash equilibria in two-player zero-sum games, rather than relying on the default maximum-entropy selection. The method achieves precise equilibrium selection (error 0.007, exploitability 5×10⁻⁵) by anchoring the reference at a target equilibrium and refining, but has limitations with off-manifold references, boundary targets, and curvature effects.
AI.motivation: In regularized self-play, when games have multiple value-equivalent equilibria, the entropy regularizer implicitly selects the maximum-entropy equilibrium. The authors ask whether this reference mechanism can be intentionally manipulated to choose a specific equilibrium on purpose, rather than leaving it to chance.
AI.method: Experiments on five exactly solvable games plus a 2-D polytope, using exact best responses and equivalence tests over independent seeds. Methods include anchoring the reference at target equilibria, refining with mirror step adjustments, comparing table-based and MLP steering maps, and testing against best response opponents.
AI.result: Anchoring the reference at a target and refining steers self-play to that member with mean coordinate error 0.007 at median exploitability 5×10⁻⁵. Selection follows the reach-weighted I-projection (slope 0.969 [0.950, 0.987]). The method persists through refinement and follows the reference, not initialization. Limitations: fixed off-manifold references cost 0.08-0.25 exploitability; boundary targets undershoot; curvature predicts boundary saturation (rank correlation 0.90, p=0.037). Table and MLP steering maps are equivalent within ±0.03. Attention's signature is excess seed variance with systematic shift bounded at 0.018.
AI.conclusion: The reference policy can serve as a deliberate equilibrium selection knob in regularized self-play, reinterpreted from RLHF as a selection mechanism rather than merely a stability leash. However, the selection-robustness trade-off is degenerate against best-response opponents—steering matters only against fixed, non-equilibrium opponents. The method has limitations with off-manifold references, boundary targets, and requires careful consideration of curvature effects.

title: Expected Hypervolume Maximization for Multiobjective Optimization under Uncertainties
summary: The problem of multiobjective optimization under uncertainties is often approached by taking the expectation of each objective. In this work, we propose instead to formulate this as a Bayesian decision problem and to rely on the expected value of the hypervolume, which is to be maximized with respect to a finite set of input points. We show that this can be performed using methods based on gradients in a stochastic optimization framework, provided that care is taken with respect to dominated points. Moreover, in the absence of readily available differentiable code, we propose to use Gaussian Processes as differentiable surrogate models, in order to perform the optimization. An additional contribution in this work are some active learning strategies, through acquisition functions which helps construct a surrogate model well-designed for the multiobjective optimization problem at stake. These strategies are compared on simple analytical problems to assess their performances.

title: BINDER: A Latent Variable Model for Probabilistic Medical Image Registration
summary: We propose a new probabilistic model for general-purpose medical image registration that builds upon the mutual information registration criterion. It centers around a spatial interpolation technique that assumes latent voxel-wise correspondences between the images being registered. By exploiting these latent variables, we derive dedicated optimization and MCMC sampling techniques that only involve closed-form iterative updates. When applied to nonlinear registration, an efficient demons-like optimization algorithm is obtained that shows robust out-of-the-box performance across a variety of monomodal and multimodal registration tasks. We also demonstrate a corresponding sampler that can quantify, for the first time, uncertainty in multimodal registration scenarios with very high-dimensional 3D deformations. Our code, which we call BINDER (Bayesian INference for DEformable Registration), is freely available at https://github.com/ste93ste/BINDER.

AI.tldr: BINDER is a new probabilistic model for general-purpose medical image registration that uses latent voxel-wise correspondences and spatial interpolation to enable closed-form iterative optimization and MCMC sampling for uncertainty quantification in multimodal registration.
AI.motivation: Medical image registration lacks robust methods that can handle both monomodal and multimodal registration tasks with uncertainty quantification. Traditional methods often struggle with multimodal images and cannot provide uncertainty estimates.
AI.method: The method introduces a spatial interpolation technique assuming latent voxel-wise correspondences between images. This allows derivation of dedicated optimization and MCMC sampling techniques involving only closed-form iterative updates. The optimization yields a demons-like algorithm, while the sampler enables uncertainty quantification.
AI.result: The demons-like optimization algorithm shows robust out-of-the-box performance across various monomodal and multimodal registration tasks. The corresponding sampler can quantify uncertainty in multimodal registration scenarios with very high-dimensional 3D deformations.
AI.conclusion: BINDER provides both efficient optimization and uncertainty quantification for deformable medical image registration, working robustly across monomodal and multimodal modalities. The code is freely available.

title: Dual-Axis Policy Optimization for LLM Agents: Bayesian Feedback Attribution and Trajectory Mass Normalization
summary: Reinforcement learning for LLM agents involves two distinct optimization di- mensions: how environment feedback is exploited within a trajectory, and how complete trajectories are aggregated across a batch. We formulate these dimen- sions as Intra-Trajectory Feedback Attribution and Inter-Trajectory Objec- tive Aggregation, and introduce BATON (Bayesian Attribution and Trajectory Objective Normalization), a dual-axis policy optimization framework. BATON instantiates the first axis with Bayesian Feedback Attribution, which constructs a feedback-conditioned posterior over sampled actions, and the second with Trajec- tory Mass Normalization (TMN), which assigns equal optimization mass to com- plete trajectories. Experiments with GRPO and GiGPO on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA show that both axes provide independent gains and that their combi- nation consistently achieves the strongest overall performance across model scales.

AI.tldr: BATON is a dual-axis policy optimization framework for LLM agents that addresses two key dimensions in reinforcement learning: how to attribute feedback within a trajectory (Intra-Trajectory Feedback Attribution) and how to aggregate across complete trajectories (Inter-Trajectory Objective Aggregation). It combines Bayesian Feedback Attribution with Trajectory Mass Normalization (TMN) to achieve consistent performance gains across model scales.
AI.motivation: Current reinforcement learning methods for LLM agents treat feedback attribution and trajectory aggregation as entangled problems, lacking principled ways to separately address how environment feedback is exploited within a trajectory versus how complete trajectories are aggregated across batches. This work aims to disentangle these two optimization dimensions.
AI.method: BATON introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) Bayesian Feedback Attribution, which constructs a feedback-conditioned posterior over sampled actions to better attribute environment feedback within trajectories, and (2) Trajectory Mass Normalization (TMN), which assigns equal optimization mass to complete trajectories to ensure balanced contribution from all sampled trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA using GRPO and GiGPO show that both axes provide independent performance gains, and their combination achieves the strongest overall performance across different model scales.
AI.conclusion: The two dimensions of Intra-Trajectory Feedback Attribution and Inter-Trajectory Objective Aggregation are complementary and orthogonal; combining Bayesian Feedback Attribution with Trajectory Mass Normalization consistently yields the best performance, demonstrating the value of separately addressing both optimization dimensions in LLM agent training.

title: Pretrained Medical Representations for the Practical Screening of Drug Repositioning Candidates
comment: Accepted at ICML 2026 AI for Science Workshop
summary: Representation learning from medical code sequences in electronic health records and medical claims data has been successful in various clinical applications, such as those regarding disease prediction. However, significant challenges remain in extending this approach to the discovery of scientific hypotheses. One reason is that many existing BERT-based models fail to adequately capture the hierarchical structure of medical codes and the complex interactions between diagnoses and treatments. To address these limitations, we propose a new unified pre-training framework that explicitly integrates hierarchical sub-token aggregation, partial masking, and cross-reference mechanisms. The proposed model consistently outperformed existing methods on both pre-training objectives and downstream clinical event prediction tasks, including the onset of dementia and hospitalization. We also conducted an in silico drug repositioning case study targeting Alzheimer's disease. In the hypothesis generation step, our approach successfully rediscovered known promising drugs in a data-driven manner without relying on such external knowledge sources as the literature. Subsequently, in the hypothesis prioritization step, we introduced a Task-Adaptive Representation Approach to alleviate the over-encoding of historical prescription information within diagnostic vectors, enabling the robust prioritization of generated hypotheses. This study establishes an exploratory screening workflow for hypothesis generation and prioritization based on observational associations. Importantly, this framework is not intended to provide causal evidence, but rather to identify promising candidates for subsequent rigorous causal inference. Overall, this study demonstrates that domain-informed representation learning combined with task-adaptive representation control can enable a practical hypothesis discovery workflow.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified pre-training framework for medical code representation learning that integrates hierarchical sub-token aggregation, partial masking, and cross-reference mechanisms. The model outperforms existing methods in clinical event prediction and enables a practical hypothesis discovery workflow for drug repositioning, particularly targeting Alzheimer's disease.
AI.motivation: Existing BERT-based models for medical code representation fail to adequately capture: 1) the hierarchical structure of medical codes, and 2) the complex interactions between diagnoses and treatments. This limits their application in scientific hypothesis discovery from EHR and medical claims data.
AI.method: The proposed unified pre-training framework incorporates three key mechanisms: 1) Hierarchical sub-token aggregation to capture medical code structure, 2) Partial masking for enhanced context learning, and 3) Cross-reference mechanisms to model diagnosis-treatment interactions. Additionally, a Task-Adaptive Representation Approach was introduced to alleviate over-encoding of historical prescription information within diagnostic vectors for hypothesis prioritization.
AI.result: The proposed model consistently outperformed existing methods on both pre-training objectives and downstream clinical event prediction tasks (dementia onset and hospitalization prediction). In the Alzheimer's disease drug repositioning case study, the approach successfully rediscovered known promising drugs in a data-driven manner without external literature knowledge. The Task-Adaptive Representation Approach enabled robust prioritization of generated hypotheses.
AI.conclusion: Domain-informed representation learning combined with task-adaptive representation control can enable a practical hypothesis discovery workflow for exploratory screening. The framework identifies promising candidates for subsequent rigorous causal inference, though it does not provide causal evidence itself.

title: SlugTrails: An Egocentric Benchmark for Floor Plan Localization in Large Buildings
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Preprint. Code and data: https://github.com/Head-inthe-Cloud/SlugTrails
summary: Floor-plan-based indoor visual localization enables infrastructure-free positioning, but most methods are developed and evaluated in small residential environments unlike the large public buildings of real deployment. We introduce SlugTrails, a floor plan localization benchmark for large indoor spaces under realistic egocentric sensing: $30$ Hz Aria glasses recordings across three campus buildings and six floors ($22089$ m$^2$ of floor plan outline), CAD-derived floor plans with semantic classes and circulation space masks, and trajectories aligned into the floor plan frame using laser-surveyed anchors. One protocol covers three practical ways of gathering geometry under a limited field of view -- a single walking frame, a stationary multi-view sweep, and a walking stream with odometry -- so methods designed for different regimes are compared on the same buildings and ground truth. Evaluating five representative geometric and learned systems under their native sensing configurations, we find that stock checkpoints (official released weights) are near zero on SlugTrails (at most $0.004$ R@1m30$^{\circ}$ on walking single frames), while fine-tuning on SlugTrails improves every trainable family on all three tasks (e.g., F$^3$Loc $0.0 \rightarrow 0.141$ single-frame and $0.03 \rightarrow 0.66$ sequential), with gains compounding as observations accumulate. The same fine-tuned weights also improve cross-dataset generalization on LaMAR with no LaMAR training (sequential R@1m $0.048 \rightarrow 0.143$ for F$^3$Loc and $0.063 \rightarrow 0.127$ for UnLoc), whereas train-from-scratch on SlugTrails alone stays far below fine-tuning from stock weights -- evidence that floor plan localization is currently limited by indoor data rather than by architecture. We release the dataset, protocols, and tools at https://github.com/Head-inthe-Cloud/SlugTrails.

AI.tldr: SlugTrails is a new floor plan-based indoor visual localization benchmark for large indoor spaces (22,089 m² across 3 campus buildings, 6 floors), featuring egocentric sensing from Aria glasses. The benchmark evaluates three practical data gathering protocols and five representative localization systems, revealing that stock pretrained models fail but fine-tuning significantly improves performance and cross-dataset generalization.
AI.motivation: Most floor-plan-based indoor visual localization methods are developed and evaluated in small residential environments, unlike real-world large public buildings. There was no appropriate benchmark for realistic large-scale indoor spaces.
AI.method: Dataset: 30 Hz Aria glasses recordings across 3 campus buildings and 6 floors with CAD-derived floor plans (semantic classes and circulation space masks). Trajectories aligned using laser-surveyed anchors. Evaluation: Three data gathering protocols (single walking frame, stationary multi-view sweep, walking stream with odometry).
