AI.conclusion: The wording of questions significantly affects VLM robustness through attention-based spectral filtering. Verbose paraphrasing is an effective strategy to improve robustness, while fine-grained questions should be avoided in corrupted environments. The proposed prompt padding method offers a simple practical solution.

title: MAGMA-GEN: Validated Recovery Supervision from Ambiguous Failures via Counterfactual Re-Execution
summary: Hierarchical robotic systems executing long-horizon manipulation tasks must make high-level semantic decisions that orchestrate stochastic low-level skills. In this setting, failed rollouts are ambiguous: a poor downstream state may reflect an invalid high-level decision, partial observation, or a valid decision whose physical execution failed. Traditional supervised learning lacks data for such recovery states, while reinforcement learning struggles with sparse rewards and non-local credit assignment. We propose MAGMA-GEN, an on-policy data-generation pipeline that converts ambiguous failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision. MAGMA-GEN first uses a privileged coach to hypothesize an early decision-level error and propose localized correction or recovery actions. Because this diagnosis is fallible, candidates are retained only if re-execution from the same state under matched conditions improves downstream progress. This produces supervised examples from the agent's own failure distribution without per-step human demonstrations. Evaluated on interactive long-horizon manipulation tasks, MAGMA-GEN improves task success and recovery capabilities, against distillation and trajectory-repair baselines under evolving task constraints in both simulation and real-robot execution.

AI.tldr: MAGMA-GEN is an on-policy data-generation pipeline for hierarchical robotic systems that converts ambiguous failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision, using a privileged coach to diagnose decision-level errors and propose recovery actions, then retaining only candidates that improve downstream progress when re-executed.
AI.motivation: In hierarchical robotic systems executing long-horizon manipulation tasks, failed rollouts are ambiguous—they may result from invalid high-level decisions, partial observation, or failed physical execution. Traditional supervised learning lacks data for recovery states, while reinforcement learning struggles with sparse rewards and non-local credit assignment.
AI.method: MAGMA-GEN uses a privileged coach to hypothesize early decision-level errors and propose localized correction or recovery actions. Since this diagnosis is fallible, candidates are retained only if re-execution from the same state under matched conditions improves downstream progress. This produces supervised examples from the agent's own failure distribution without per-step human demonstrations.
AI.result: MAGMA-GEN improves task success and recovery capabilities against distillation and trajectory-repair baselines under evolving task constraints, in both simulation and real-robot execution.
AI.conclusion: MAGMA-GEN provides an effective approach for learning recovery behaviors in hierarchical robotic systems by converting failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision, eliminating the need for per-step human demonstrations while addressing the credit assignment problem in long-horizon tasks.

title: QoS-Aware Federated Learning for Multimodal In-Cabin Interaction in Smart Vehicles
summary: Modern smart vehicles leverage multimodal sensors, ranging from high-bandwidth vision systems to low-rate physiological monitors, to provide personalized in-cabin services. However, integrating high-fidelity multimodal fusion with collaborative training is often hindered by the heterogeneous and time-varying Quality of Service (QoS) constraints of vehicular networks. Standard Federated Learning (FL) approaches enforce rigid synchronous rounds that fail to account for these resource asymmetries, leading to safety-critical timing violations and energy exhaustion. In this paper, we propose FedQoS, a novel asynchronous, event-triggered FL framework that decouples local computation from global communication via a two-phase gating mechanism. First, we introduce a resource-aware training gate that initializes local learning only when sensing buffers and energy reserves meet safety thresholds, preventing ML tasks from compromising core vehicle mobility. Second, a QoS-aware transmission policy gates uplink updates based on an efficiency score that balances model novelty against instantaneous latency and energy costs. Locally, clients optimize an objective featuring a staleness-aware proximal term that dynamically adjusts the global anchor strength based on update age. Extensive experiments on multimodal vehicular datasets demonstrate that FedQoS achieves competitive personalized accuracy with only marginal performance loss compared to FedAvg, while substantially reducing QoS violations, cutting communication overhead by 76.7\%, and lowering latency cost by 26.0\%, demonstrating a highly favorable accuracy and efficiency balance for real-world vehicular deployments.

AI.tldr: FedQoS is a novel asynchronous, event-triggered Federated Learning framework designed for modern smart vehicles with multimodal sensors. It uses a two-phase gating mechanism (resource-aware training gate and QoS-aware transmission policy) to decouple local computation from global communication, addressing the heterogeneous QoS constraints of vehicular networks.
AI.motivation: Modern smart vehicles leverage multimodal sensors for personalized in-cabin services, but integrating high-fidelity multimodal fusion with collaborative training is hindered by heterogeneous and time-varying QoS constraints in vehicular networks. Standard FL approaches enforce rigid synchronous rounds that fail to account for resource asymmetries, leading to safety-critical timing violations and energy exhaustion.
AI.method: FedQoS proposes a two-phase gating mechanism: (1) Resource-aware training gate that initializes local learning only when sensing buffers and energy reserves meet safety thresholds; (2) QoS-aware transmission policy that gates uplink updates based on an efficiency score balancing model novelty against latency and energy costs. Additionally, clients optimize an objective featuring a staleness-aware proximal term that dynamically adjusts the global anchor strength based on update age.
AI.result: FedQoS achieves competitive personalized accuracy with only marginal performance loss compared to FedAvg, while substantially reducing QoS violations, cutting communication overhead by 76.7%, and lowering latency cost by 26.0%.
AI.conclusion: FedQoS demonstrates a highly favorable accuracy and efficiency balance for real-world vehicular deployments, effectively addressing the challenges of asynchronous FL in heterogeneous vehicular network environments.

title: Bridging Modalities on the Cortex: Surface-based MRI to PET Translation with a Diffusion Bridge
summary: Cortical hypometabolism measured by Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography (FDG-PET) is a highly sensitive biomarker for dementia diagnosis. However, high costs, radiation exposure, and limited accessibility constrain its clinical utility. While cross-modal synthesis from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers a promising alternative, existing volumetric generation methods do not explicitly account for the highly folded cortical geometry, where disease-related patterns predominantly reside. To address this, we introduce a novel surface-based diffusion bridge framework DB-SUiT for MRI-to-PET translation that operates natively on the cortical manifold. A conditional Spherical U-shaped vision Transformer (SUiT) is specifically designed to model the intricate cross-modal relationships while preserving surface topology. It combines spherical convolutional encoders for multi-scale surface feature extraction with bottleneck Transformers to capture long-range spatial dependencies, while incorporating demographic and subcortical conditions to refine the synthesis. Evaluated on two datasets, including subjects with different dementia types, DB-SUiT demonstrates high-fidelity synthesis that substantially outperforms other baselines. In automated dementia classification, synthesized PET surfaces improve performance over MRI by 14.2% and PET volumes by 11.3%, approaching the performance of real PET surfaces. In a blinded reader study, synthetic PET achieved 85.5% diagnostic accuracy, compared with 75.8% for MRI and 95.2% for real PET. This further demonstrates cross-cohort and cross-pathology generalization, as the model was evaluated without retraining on an external cohort that included a dementia subtype not represented during training. Our code is available at https://github.com/ai-med/DB-SUiT.

AI.tldr: DB-SUiT is a novel surface-based diffusion bridge framework for MRI-to-PET translation that operates on the cortical manifold to synthesize FDG-PET images from MRI, avoiding the costs, radiation exposure, and limited accessibility of actual PET scans while maintaining diagnostic utility for dementia classification.
AI.motivation: FDG-PET is a highly sensitive biomarker for dementia diagnosis but suffers from high costs, radiation exposure, and limited accessibility. Existing MRI-to-PET translation methods do not account for the highly folded cortical geometry where disease-related patterns predominantly reside, necessitating a surface-based approach that preserves cortical topology.
AI.method: The framework uses a conditional Spherical U-shaped vision Transformer (SUiT) that operates natively on the cortical manifold. It combines spherical convolutional encoders for multi-scale surface feature extraction with bottleneck Transformers to capture long-range spatial dependencies. Demographic and subcortical conditions are incorporated to refine synthesis. The model is evaluated on two datasets including different dementia types, with external validation on an unseen dementia subtype.
AI.result: DB-SUiT substantially outperforms other baselines in high-fidelity synthesis. In automated dementia classification, synthesized PET surfaces improve performance over MRI by 14.2% and PET volumes by 11.3%, approaching real PET surface performance. In a blinded reader study, synthetic PET achieved 85.5% diagnostic accuracy vs. 75.8% for MRI and 95.2% for real PET. The model demonstrates cross-cohort and cross-pathology generalization without retraining on an external cohort with a previously unseen dementia subtype.
AI.conclusion: DB-SUiT successfully synthesizes diagnostically valuable PET images from MRI using surface-based deep learning, achieving near-real-PET performance while eliminating radiation exposure and reducing costs. The approach shows strong generalization across different cohorts and dementia subtypes, making it a promising clinical tool for accessible dementia diagnosis.

title: WiCleanData: Guaranteeing the Type Consistency of Wikidata by Taxonomy Refinement and Constraint Enforcement
summary: Because of its collaborative nature, Wikidata suffers from errors, in- consistencies, and excessive complexity, such as redundant classes, ambiguity between instances and classes, wrong taxonomic paths, and type constraint violations. The manual curation of these issues is infeasible at scale. To address these challenges, we introduce WiCleanData, a refined version of Wikidata with a consistent tax- onomy and free from type constraint violations. Specifically, we have designed an automated pipeline that first cleans the taxonomy with language model assistance, then simplifies type constraints by hierarchical aggregation, and finally filters facts accordingly. The resulting knowledge graph, free from any type violation, is made publicly available via a Web interface, enabling easy exploration and downstream applications.

AI.tldr: WiCleanData is a refined version of Wikidata that addresses errors, inconsistencies, and complexity issues through an automated pipeline, resulting in a knowledge graph with consistent taxonomy and no type constraint violations.
AI.motivation: Wikidata suffers from quality issues due to its collaborative nature, including errors, inconsistencies, redundant classes, ambiguity between instances and classes, wrong taxonomic paths, and type constraint violations. Manual curation is infeasible at scale.
AI.method: The paper proposes an automated pipeline with three stages: (1) taxonomy cleaning with language model assistance, (2) type constraint simplification through hierarchical aggregation, and (3) fact filtering based on the cleaned constraints.
AI.result: The resulting knowledge graph is free from type constraint violations and is made publicly available via a Web interface for exploration and downstream applications.
AI.conclusion: WiCleanData provides a cleaned, consistent version of Wikidata that enables easier exploration and supports downstream applications without the original quality issues.

title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
summary: Deployment-time safety methods for large language models (LLMs) are predominantly supervised and assume access to unsafe training data. Nevertheless, new attacks and harm categories regularly arise, not captured by models trained in such a supervised fashion. An alternative approach is to view this problem through the lens of anomaly detection, namely, to rely solely on modeling safe data and flagging out-of-distribution inputs. However, LLM activations lie in a high-dimensional space, raising concerns about whether anomaly detection is statistically feasible. We show that, under the linear representation hypothesis (LRH), there may indeed be hope. In the LRH concept space, which is typically recovered via a sparse autoencoder (SAE), nearby points share a small common active support. Using this local sparsity insight, we propose a framework for locally masked SAE-based anomaly detection, supported by theoretical justifications. We validate it on various architectures and datasets, including both capability-testing datasets and safety-specific datasets. Finally, when we allow algorithms to use 1% out-of-distribution data for calibration, locally sparse methods achieve near-optimal performance, demonstrating their ability to capture meaningful safety information while using only 1-2% of SAE neurons for computation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel anomaly detection framework for LLM safety using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) and local sparsity properties under the linear representation hypothesis. The method identifies out-of-distribution (potentially harmful) inputs by modeling only safe data, achieving near-optimal performance with just 1% OOD calibration data and only 1-2% of SAE neurons.
AI.motivation: Current supervised safety methods require unsafe training data, which is problematic because new attacks and harm categories continuously emerge. While anomaly detection using only safe data is a potential solution, the high-dimensional nature of LLM activations raises feasibility concerns. This work addresses this challenge by leveraging the linear representation hypothesis and local sparsity properties of SAE representations.
AI.method: The proposed framework uses locally masked SAE-based anomaly detection. Based on the insight that under LRH, nearby points in concept space share a small common active support, the method performs anomaly detection locally within the SAE representation space. This approach is supported by theoretical justifications and requires only 1-2% of SAE neurons for computation.
AI.result: The method was validated on various architectures and datasets, including both capability-testing and safety-specific datasets. When using 1% out-of-distribution data for calibration, locally sparse methods achieve near-optimal performance, demonstrating meaningful safety information capture with minimal computational resources.
AI.conclusion: The local sparsity insight provides a viable path for anomaly detection in high-dimensional LLM activation spaces. This approach successfully balances safety detection with computational efficiency, using only 1-2% of SAE neurons while achieving near-optimal performance with minimal calibration data.

title: Task-Oriented Semantic Feature Transmission for Multi-Task Satellite Remote Sensing over Low-SNR Channels
summary: Conventional satellite remote sensing transmission follows a reconstruct-then-infer paradigm that optimizes pixel-level fidelity, creating an objective mismatch with downstream tasks such as classification and detection, especially at low SNR. This paper investigates a task-oriented framework that bypasses image reconstruction and directly transmits semantic features extracted by a multitask-pretrained backbone. A lightweight channel adaptation module (CAM) compresses feature dimensionality for bandwidth reduction, and a feature restorer recovers task-relevant structure after channel corruption. With the backbone frozen, the CAM and task-specific downstream heads are jointly optimized with task and feature-level supervision under random-SNR training. Under the adopted AWGN setting, experiments on scene classification and object detection show consistent gains over reconstruction-oriented JSCC baselines across different SNR conditions, with the largest improvements in the low-SNR regime.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a task-oriented semantic communication framework for satellite remote sensing that bypasses traditional image reconstruction, instead transmitting compressed semantic features directly for downstream classification and detection tasks.
AI.motivation: Conventional satellite transmission follows a "reconstruct-then-infer" paradigm that optimizes pixel-level fidelity, which creates an objective mismatch with downstream tasks like classification and detection, especially at low SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio). The authors aim to address this limitation by developing a task-oriented framework.
AI.method: The framework uses: (1) a multitask-pretrained backbone to extract semantic features, (2) a lightweight Channel Adaptation Module (CAM) to compress feature dimensionality for bandwidth reduction, and (3) a feature restorer to recover task-relevant structure after channel corruption. With the backbone frozen, the CAM and task-specific downstream heads are jointly optimized with task and feature-level supervision under random-SNR training in an AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) setting.
AI.result: Experiments on scene classification and object detection show consistent gains over reconstruction-oriented JSCC (Joint Source-Channel Coding) baselines across different SNR conditions, with the largest improvements occurring in the low-SNR regime.
AI.conclusion: The proposed task-oriented semantic communication framework effectively addresses the objective mismatch problem in satellite remote sensing transmission, particularly excelling in low-SNR conditions where traditional reconstruction-based methods struggle.

title: FCA-Guided Counterfactual Explanations for Multi-Modal Breast Cancer Diagnosis: A Framework Achieving Perfect Validity with Emergent Sparsity
summary: Deep learning models for multi-modal breast cancer diagnosis achieve high predictive accuracy but remain clinically unacceptable without actionable, counterfactual explanations. Attribution-based methods (LIME, SHAP) are categorically inapplicable to this purpose, as they generate no alternative instances and thus cannot be evaluated on counterfactual quality metrics. This investigation provides empirical evidence that FCA-Guided Counterfactual (FCA-CF) framework that uses a Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) concept lattice as a hard structural constraint on counterfactual search, operating over a multi-modal TCGA-BRCA dataset. We benchmark against four genuine counterfactual methods: Wachter-style CF, DiCE, FACE, and NICE, evaluated on 60 benign-predicted TCGA-BRCA instances. The FCA-CF framework achieves Validity = 1.0000 (100% of counterfactuals successfully flip the prediction), Sparsity = 2.37 features changed (best among all valid methods), and Proximity = 0.900 (normalised L2-based, matching NICE as joint best). The classifier achieves Accuracy = 0.980, F1 = 0.976, ROC-AUC = 0.9947. Ablation analysis confirms that the FCA lattice constraint is the primary sparsity driver (removing it increases sparsity by +40%, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.78), while Phase C greedy refinement accounts for the largest individual contribution (+113% sparsity increase when disabled, p < 0.001, d = 5.01). FCA-guided counterfactual generation achieves a clinically important Pareto-dominant outcome; it is simultaneously the sparsest and among the most proximate of all valid methods, with perfect validity. The emergent sparsity property arising from lattice topology rather than numerical penalty terms constitutes a structurally novel contribution to the counterfactual explanation literature.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes FCA-CF, a counterfactual explanation framework for multi-modal breast cancer diagnosis that uses Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) concept lattice as a structural constraint. The framework achieves perfect validity (100%), best sparsity (2.37 features changed), and competitive proximity (0.900), while the classifier achieves 98% accuracy. Ablation studies confirm the FCA lattice constraint as the primary driver of sparsity.
AI.motivation: Deep learning models for breast cancer diagnosis achieve high predictive accuracy but lack actionable, counterfactual explanations. Existing attribution-based methods (LIME, SHAP) cannot generate alternative instances and thus cannot be evaluated on counterfactual quality metrics, making them clinically inadequate.
AI.method: The FCA-CF framework uses Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) concept lattice as a hard structural constraint on counterfactual search, operating over a multi-modal TCGA-BRCA dataset. The method is benchmarked against four genuine counterfactual methods: Wachter-style CF, DiCE, FACE, and NICE, evaluated on 60 benign-predicted TCGA-BRCA instances.
AI.result: FCA-CF achieves Validity = 1.0000 (100% flip rate), Sparsity = 2.37 features changed (best among all valid methods), and Proximity = 0.900 (joint best with NICE). The classifier achieves Accuracy = 0.980, F1 = 0.976, ROC-AUC = 0.9947. Ablation analysis shows that removing the FCA lattice constraint increases sparsity by +40% (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.78), while disabling Phase C greedy refinement increases sparsity by +113% (p < 0.001, d = 5.01).
AI.conclusion: FCA-guided counterfactual generation achieves a Pareto-dominant outcome: it is simultaneously the sparsest and among the most proximate of all valid methods, with perfect validity. The emergent sparsity property arises from lattice topology rather than numerical penalty terms, constituting a structurally novel contribution to the counterfactual explanation literature.

title: Fast-varying Natural Frequencies and Damping Ratio Identification for Linear Time-Varying System
comment: Preprint submitted to Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing
summary: This work proposes a physics-enhanced machine learning approach for the system identification of Linear Time-Varying (LTV) systems under time-varying operating conditions in terms of fast-varying natural frequencies and damping ratios by combining a long short-term memory network with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). The proposed approach uses vibration data (displacement and velocity measurements), domain knowledge of modal damping ratios, and a physics-based model that can yield an approximate natural frequencies time-dependency model. The approach is validated using synthetic data generated from a finite element model of a 2-blade offshore wind turbine under realistic environmental and operating conditions. This system displays fast time-varying frequencies due to operating conditions, whose identification is particularly challenging because of the wind and wave loading. The robustness of the proposed approach is assessed under assumed incorrect system information (e.g. damping ratio). The proposed approach is evaluated across different environmental and operating conditions to show its applicability to different operating regimes. The results show the approach can accurately identify the selected fast-varying natural frequency, 1st Fore-Aft (FA-1) mode, with a maximum root mean square error of 0.0012 Hz. The results demonstrate that the model trained on EKF estimates depends on accurate damping values, whereas the model trained on physics-based data exhibits robustness to incorrect damping assumptions. The approach is extended to damping ratio identification for the selected mode by estimating the root mean square error between models trained on EKF estimates and physics-based data. The results show that the approach can yield a good approximation of the FA-1 mode damping ratio using grid search, offering an improvement over covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification.

AI.tldr: A physics-enhanced machine learning approach combining LSTM networks with Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for system identification of Linear Time-Varying (LTV) systems, specifically applied to a 2-blade offshore wind turbine to identify fast-varying natural frequencies and damping ratios under time-varying operating conditions.
AI.motivation: The identification of fast-varying natural frequencies and damping ratios in Linear Time-Varying (LTV) systems under time-varying operating conditions (e.g., wind and wave loading) is particularly challenging. Current methods struggle with the dynamic nature of systems like offshore wind turbines, where environmental conditions cause rapid changes in modal properties.
AI.method: The proposed approach combines a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). It integrates: (1) vibration data (displacement and velocity measurements), (2) domain knowledge of modal damping ratios, and (3) a physics-based model for approximate natural frequency time-dependency. The method is validated using synthetic data from a finite element model of a 2-blade offshore wind turbine under realistic environmental and operating conditions. Robustness is assessed under incorrect system information (e.g., damping ratio), and the approach is extended to damping ratio identification using grid search.
AI.result: The approach accurately identifies the 1st Fore-Aft (FA-1) mode natural frequency with a maximum RMSE of 0.0012 Hz. The model trained on EKF estimates requires accurate damping values, while the model trained on physics-based data shows robustness to incorrect damping assumptions. The damping ratio identification using grid search yields good approximation and outperforms covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification.
AI.conclusion: The physics-enhanced LSTM-EKF approach effectively identifies fast-varying natural frequencies in LTV systems. The physics-based training data provides robustness to damping assumptions, making it practical for real-world applications. The method can also estimate damping ratios, offering an improvement over traditional subspace identification methods.

title: Ischemic Stroke Segmentation and Net Water Uptake Quantification on Multicenter Non-Contrast CT Using Supervised Target-Domain Adaptation
summary:
Objectives: Quantitative assessment of infarct hypodensity on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), including net water uptake (NWU), requires manual or semi-manual lesion delineation, often guided by CT perfusion or diffusion-weighted MRI, limiting clinical applicability. Automated segmentation on NCCT could enable efficient biomarker extraction such as NWU but remains challenging across heterogeneous multicenter data. This study aimed to develop and externally test a domain-aware deep learning framework for ischemic stroke segmentation on NCCT and assess its suitability for NWU quantification.
  Materials & Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study of 801 patients from four datasets, an nnU-Net-based model was trained on NCCT scans from the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf and the Acute Ischemic Stroke Dataset. To adapt to new domains, the model was fine-tuned on target-domain subsets from Boston (n=11) and ISLES (n=75), with evaluation on held-out cases not used for fine-tuning. Automated segmentations and NWU values were compared with expert references.
  Results: For lesions $\geq$ 30 mL, median Dice was 0.68 (Boston) and 0.56 (ISLES). Including smaller lesions, which predominated in ISLES, median Dice was 0.54 (interquartile range [IQR] 0.30-0.70) for acute lesion segmentation (Boston dataset) and 0.20 (IQR 0.03-0.41) for NCCT lesion segmentations when compared to post-treatment infarct (primary target of the ISLES challenge). Automated NWU mean absolute error was 1.37 percentage points (SD 1.61, Boston).
  Conclusion: Target-domain adaptation supported NCCT-only infarct segmentation across heterogeneous external cohorts, although performance varied across domains. The approach enabled low-error NWU quantification from baseline NCCT without advanced imaging, supporting further prospective clinical evaluation.

AI.tldr: This study developed a domain-aware deep learning framework (nnU-Net-based) for automated ischemic stroke segmentation on non-contrast CT (NCCT) and evaluated its suitability for quantifying net water uptake (NWU) across heterogeneous multicenter data. The model was trained on 801 patients from four datasets and achieved moderate to good segmentation accuracy (Dice 0.68 for lesions ≥30mL in Boston, 0.56 in ISLES) with NWU quantification error of 1.37 percentage points.
AI.motivation: Current quantitative assessment of infarct hypodensity on NCCT (including NWU) requires manual or semi-manual lesion delineation, often guided by CT perfusion or diffusion-weighted MRI, limiting clinical applicability. An automated segmentation tool could enable efficient biomarker extraction but faces challenges across heterogeneous multicenter data.
AI.method: Retrospective multicenter study using an nnU-Net-based model trained on NCCT scans from University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf and Acute Ischemic Stroke Dataset. Target-domain adaptation was performed by fine-tuning on subsets from Boston (n=11) and ISLES (n=75), with evaluation on held-out cases not used for fine-tuning. Automated segmentations and NWU values were compared with expert references.
AI.result: For lesions ≥30 mL, median Dice was 0.68 (Boston) and 0.56 (ISLES). Including smaller lesions, median Dice was 0.54 (IQR 0.30-0.70) for Boston and 0.20 (IQR 0.03-0.41) for ISLES (compared to post-treatment infarct). Automated NWU mean absolute error was 1.37 percentage points (SD 1.61, Boston).
AI.conclusion: Target-domain adaptation enabled NCCT-only infarct segmentation across heterogeneous external cohorts, though performance varied across domains. The approach enabled low-error NWU quantification from baseline NCCT without advanced imaging, supporting further prospective clinical evaluation.

title: Marginal utility, matrix factorization, and the Key-Value (KV) cache: a unified information-economic framework for sovereign geo-mining inference
comment: Version 11, 14 septembre 2026. 49 pages, 9 tables. Les valeurs de l'architecture souveraine sont projet{é}es et non mesur{é}es ; le calcul {à} grande {é}chelle est en cours. Soumission pr{é}vue {à} IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
summary: This paper builds a theoretical bridge between the economic notion of marginal utility and two machine-learning constructs, matrix factorization and the Key--Value cache of transformer language models. The singular value spectrum of a rating matrix is shown to be a diminishing marginal utility schedule for latent factors, the eigenvalue spectrum of the projected covariance operator to be the marginal utility schedule of a model's learned representation, and cache eviction and low-rank cache compression to be instances of constrained utility maximization under a memory budget. The three collapse into a single allocation rule: retain the top dimensions whose eigenvalue exceeds the shadow price of the binding constraint. The framework is applied to the automated extraction of structured information from geo-mining documents, where it motivates a multi-pass inference protocol, a layer-wise TIES model merging procedure, and a selection policy combining extraction quality, localization drift and energy, scalarized with a Conditional Value-at-Risk term on drift. Two empirical contributions are reported. An 11.2-million-parameter hierarchical classifier, trained in about five minutes on a single GPU, reaches 90.0 per cent level-1 accuracy on a held-out test set from a 973-document uranium-exploration corpus, against 92.0 per cent for a proprietary model on a fifty-document human audit of the same corpus, at a latency of 2.62 ms per card against approximately 2,000 ms for the API and at negligible cost. A diagnostic of uniform-density TIES merging exposes a reproducible degenerate mode in which the merged model returns token-identical outputs across five geographically distinct districts while declaring high confidence; re-executing the merge under layer-wise calibrated densities removes that signature on the diagnostic sample. The full-scale extraction benchmark, including LoRA fine-tuning, is reported as projected rather than measured and remains an empirical extension of this work.

AI.tldr: This paper bridges economic marginal utility theory with machine learning constructs (matrix factorization and transformer KV cache), deriving a unified allocation rule for retaining dimensions whose eigenvalue exceeds the shadow price of constraints. It applies this framework to geo-mining document extraction, achieving 90% accuracy with 2.62ms latency using an 11.2M parameter model trained in 5 minutes. A diagnostic reveals a degenerate mode in uniform-density TIES merging that is resolved by layer-wise calibrated densities.
AI.motivation: To build a theoretical connection between economic marginal utility and machine learning constructs (matrix factorization, KV cache), addressing optimal resource allocation in latent factor models and transformer memory management under constraints.
AI.method: Theoretical framework: (1) Mapping singular value spectrum to marginal utility schedule for latent factors; (2) Mapping eigenvalue spectrum of covariance operator to marginal utility of learned representations; (3) Formulating cache eviction/compression as constrained utility maximization. Applications: multi-pass inference protocol, layer-wise TIES model merging, and a selection policy with CVaR term on drift. Empirical validation on uranium-exploration corpus with 11.2M parameter hierarchical classifier.
AI.result: The 11.2M parameter model achieves 90.0% level-1 accuracy on 973-document test set (vs 92.0% for proprietary model on 50-document audit), with 2.62ms latency vs ~2000ms for API, trained in ~5 minutes on single GPU. Uniform-density TIES merging produces a reproducible degenerate mode (token-identical outputs across 5 districts with high confidence), eliminated by layer-wise calibrated densities.
AI.conclusion: The marginal utility framework provides a unifying principle for dimension retention, cache management, and model merging. The approach delivers strong accuracy-latency tradeoffs for geo-mining document extraction. However, uniform-density merging introduces degenerate behavior requiring careful calibration. Full-scale extraction benchmark remains projected rather than measured.

title: QUALS: Corpus Equilibrium for Universal Forecasting via Pattern Quantization and Learnability Synchronization
summary: Ubiquitous time series data across diverse domains enables critical applications in areas such as transportation systems and power grids. Recently, training foundation models on massive datasets to achieve accurate zero-shot forecasting has emerged as a major research focus. However, current studies predominantly prioritize architectural innovations while insufficiently addressing data diversity, often relying on simple data sampling strategies that fail to manage complex data distributions effectively, leading to inefficient use of training data and suboptimal performance. To address this, we propose QUALS, a large-scale time series corpus equilibrium framework. QUALS significantly enhances data efficiency, i.e., enabling existing models to achieve superior performance using only a small fraction of the original training data. Specifically, QUALS operates through two core mechanisms. First, a pattern quantization framework systematically decodes heterogeneous patterns from mixed corpora via vector quantization and uniform binning. Second, a learnability synchronization framework calibrates sampling weights for heterogeneous patterns, bridging the optimization gap between simple and complex motifs to maximize overall training efficiency. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that pre-training on QUALS consistently achieves superior zero-shot performance, even under substantially reduced training budgets.

AI.tldr: QUALS is a large-scale time series corpus equilibrium framework that enhances data efficiency in training foundation models for zero-shot forecasting. It uses pattern quantization (vector quantization + uniform binning) and learnability synchronization (calibrating sampling weights) to address the problem of inefficient data usage caused by simple sampling strategies that fail to handle complex data distributions.
AI.motivation: Current time series foundation models prioritize architectural innovations but neglect data diversity management. Simple data sampling strategies fail to handle complex data distributions effectively, leading to inefficient use of training data and suboptimal zero-shot forecasting performance.
AI.method: QUALS employs two core mechanisms: (1) Pattern quantization framework - systematically decodes heterogeneous patterns from mixed corpora via vector quantization and uniform binning; (2) Learnability synchronization framework - calibrates sampling weights for heterogeneous patterns to bridge the optimization gap between simple and complex motifs.
AI.result: QUALS significantly enhances data efficiency, enabling existing models to achieve superior performance using only a small fraction of the original training data. Pre-training on QUALS consistently achieves superior zero-shot performance even under substantially reduced training budgets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed QUALS framework effectively addresses data diversity issues in time series foundation model training by balancing heterogeneous patterns through quantization and learnability-based sampling, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot forecasting performance with improved data efficiency.

title: Needles in a Raystack: Ultra-Sparse LiDAR Occupancy Detection for Bat Tracks
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Accepted and presented at the AI4Nature@AVSS 2026 Workshop of the 22nd International Conference on Advanced Visual and Signal-Based Systems (AVSS 2026), Lecce, Italy
summary:
Monitoring flying animals is important for understanding and protecting biodiversity, but nocturnal species such as bats are difficult to observe in the field. Using LiDAR, bat movements at night result in ultra-sparse 3D spatio-temporal data in which standard reconstruction losses tend to predict only background and miss real flight paths. We study this problem as voxel-wise occupancy detection in sensor-centric LiDAR raystacks. A lightweight 3D U-Net is proposed that preserves temporal resolution, uses skip connections for spatial detail, and combines weighted binary cross-entropy with Dice loss to handle the strong class imbalance.
  In real LiDAR recordings of bats over open fields, cross-checked with acoustic monitoring, a reconstruction-based 3D convolutional autoencoder baseline fails to recover foreground trajectories. In contrast, the proposed U-Net recovers sparse foreground occupancy in diagnostic experiments and produces coherent occupancy patterns along bat flight trajectories, providing a practical basis for validation-scale experiments, later clustering of flight tracks, and future integration of bat activity information into biodiversity-aware turbine curtailment strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of monitoring nocturnal bats using LiDAR, which produces ultra-sparse 3D data where standard reconstruction methods fail to detect actual flight paths. The authors propose a lightweight 3D U-Net approach for voxel-wise occupancy detection that handles class imbalance through combined weighted BCE and Dice loss.
AI.motivation: Monitoring flying animals, especially nocturnal species like bats, is crucial for biodiversity understanding and protection, but traditional field observation methods are ineffective at night. LiDAR offers a potential solution but produces extremely sparse data where standard deep learning approaches only predict background and miss real flight trajectories.
AI.method: The proposed approach treats bat detection as a voxel-wise occupancy detection problem in sensor-centric LiDAR raystacks. A lightweight 3D U-Net architecture is used with: (1) preservation of temporal resolution, (2) skip connections for spatial detail, and (3) a hybrid loss combining weighted binary cross-entropy with Dice loss to handle the severe class imbalance between foreground (bats) and background.
AI.result: In real LiDAR recordings of bats over open fields (validated with acoustic monitoring), a reconstruction-based 3D convolutional autoencoder baseline completely fails to recover foreground trajectories. The proposed U-Net successfully recovers sparse foreground occupancy in diagnostic experiments and produces coherent occupancy patterns along bat flight trajectories.
AI.conclusion: The U-Net approach provides a practical solution for bat detection in LiDAR data, enabling validation-scale experiments, flight track clustering, and potential integration into biodiversity-aware turbine curtailment strategies to reduce bat mortality from wind turbines.

title: Tailored to you: longitudinal effects of personalising language models
summary: Interest in developing personalised language models is rapidly growing. While personalisation is often viewed as a mechanism to better serve diverse user needs, the effects of sustained interactions with personalised models on people's perception of and behaviour toward AI remain poorly understood. Most critically, downstream consequences outside the immediate human--AI interaction loop, such as effects on users' self-perceptions and interpersonal relationships, remain largely unexamined. In this study, we recruited 992 participants to complete daily advice-seeking interactions with language models over the course of five days, comparing outcomes from a non-personalised baseline against two personalisation approaches: memory-based (conditioned on prior conversational history) and survey-based (conditioned on information collected through a pre-study intake survey). We find that several changes in human-AI interaction over time are driven primarily by repeated exposure rather than personalisation itself. However, participants interacting with personalised models experienced differences in advice-seeking and information-sharing attitudes and behaviours: participants in the memory-based condition engaged in greater self-disclosure and rated the model as less creepy, while participants in the survey-based condition reported higher regret about having shared personal information with the AI. We conclude by highlighting the nuanced effects of different personalisation approaches on interaction outcomes, and discussing the implications of these findings for the responsible design and deployment of personalised AI systems.

AI.tldr: A study with 992 participants over 5 days examined how personalized language models affect human-AI interactions compared to a non-personalized baseline. Memory-based personalisation increased self-disclosure and reduced perceived creepiness, while survey-based personalisation increased regret about sharing personal information. Some effects were driven by repeated exposure rather than personalisation itself.
AI.motivation: To address the gap in understanding how sustained interactions with personalized AI systems affect users' self-perception, interpersonal relationships, and overall perception of AI, beyond immediate interaction outcomes.
AI.method: Recruited 992 participants to complete daily advice-seeking interactions with language models over five days, comparing three conditions: non-personalized baseline, memory-based personalisation (conditioned on prior conversational history), and survey-based personalisation (conditioned on pre-study intake survey information).
AI.result: Repeated exposure, not personalisation itself, drove several changes in human-AI interaction over time. However, personalisation approaches produced distinct effects: memory-based condition participants engaged in greater self-disclosure and rated the model as less creepy, while survey-based condition participants reported higher regret about sharing personal information with the AI.
AI.conclusion: Different personalisation approaches have nuanced and sometimes contradictory effects on user attitudes and behaviours. These findings highlight the importance of considering the specific type of personalisation when designing and deploying personalized AI systems, with implications for responsible AI development.

title: A Noise Optimum in Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning: Isolation, Mechanism, and Scope
summary: Injecting stochastic noise into a consolidation rule can improve a network's retention of earlier tasks up to an optimal level, then degrade it -- an inverted-U in retention vs. noise. This paper isolates what produces that optimum and maps where it holds, entirely in simulation. (1) Phenomenon: the retention inverted-U appears on several related-task continual-learning benchmarks (Split-MNIST, FashionMNIST, continual Yin-Yang). (2) Isolation: a magnitude-matched ladder shows the effect requires coherent restoring toward the consolidated weights -- a random-direction force of identical magnitude produces no optimum, and a coherent force toward the wrong target actively hurts. (3) Active ingredient: most of the optimum is recovered by coupling the anchor gain to the injected-noise variance sigma^2 -- a one-line rule that neither Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Adaptation (fixed gain) nor MESU (posterior-variance gain) implements. A forced Ornstein-Uhlenbeck calculation derives the rising flank and predicts that the optimal noise rises with per-task interference g -- confirmed out-of-sample in direction against pre-existing measurements (the exponent is unresolved at our grid). The barrier-conditioning of the originating Doob h-transform is a low-sigma safety net that bounds forgetting where the coupled gain is too weak. (4) Scope: the optimum requires shared task structure -- it is absent on permuted-MNIST, and a controlled rotated-vs-permuted comparison localizes the boundary to task structure; the precise governing quantity is left open. (5) Length: at matched severity the advantage persists but attenuates with task count, and we show no rotation family can attribute the trend (a compact-group identity). A single-seed BrainScaleS-2 demonstration of the originating rule is reported separately (Howe, arXiv:2607.06924); this paper makes no hardware claim.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates why injecting stochastic noise into weight consolidation rules produces an optimal retention level (inverted-U phenomenon) in continual learning. The key finding is that coupling anchor gain to noise variance (σ²) recovers most of the optimum, and this effect requires coherent task structure - it disappears on permuted-MNIST but appears on related-task benchmarks.
AI.motivation: The authors observed that adding stochastic noise to consolidation rules can improve network retention of earlier tasks, but only up to an optimal level - more noise degrades retention. This inverted-U relationship needed investigation to understand what produces the optimum and when it holds.
AI.method: The study uses entirely simulation-based analysis across: (1) benchmarks including Split-MNIST, FashionMNIST, and continual Yin-Yang; (2) magnitude-matched ladder experiments to isolate the mechanism; (3) deriving forced Ornstein-Uhlenbeck calculations to predict the rising flank; (4) comparing rotated-vs-permuted MNIST to localize boundaries; (5) examining task count effects with matched severity.
AI.result: Key findings: (1) The retention inverted-U appears on related-task benchmarks but not permuted-MNIST; (2) The effect requires coherent restoring toward consolidated weights - random-direction forces produce no optimum; (3) Coupling anchor gain to noise variance σ² recovers most of the optimum - a one-line rule not implemented by Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Adaptation or MESU; (4) Optimal noise rises with per-task interference g; (5) The effect attenuates with task count but persists at matched severity; (6) The barrier-conditioning of Doob h-transform provides a low-sigma safety net bounding forgetting.
AI.conclusion: The optimum requires shared task structure - it's absent on permuted-MNIST and present on related-task benchmarks. The precise governing quantity for task structure is left open. The advantage persists but attenuates with task count. A separate paper demonstrates the originating rule on BrainScaleS-2 hardware (Howe, arXiv:2607.06924).

title: MTF-Net: Multi-Modal Temporal Feature Fusion Network for Pedestrian Intention Prediction
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, accepted on International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing
summary: Accurately predicting pedestrian intentions is crucial for ensuring safe and proactive interaction between autonomous vehicles and pedestrians. However, existing approaches often depend on architectures that either model temporal dependencies within individual modalities or fuse modalities only at coarse semantic levels. To address these limitations, we propose MTF-Net, a novel Multi-Modal Temporal Feature Fusion Network that jointly models kinematic, appearance, and contextual cues for pedestrian intention prediction. MTF-Net integrates four complementary modalities-bounding-box dynamics, human pose keypoints, local context, and scene-level semantics within a recurrent fusion framework enhanced by gated linear units (GLUs). These GLU-based modules adaptively regulate cross-modal information flow, enabling interpretable and efficient feature interaction across temporal scales. Through three dedicated temporal encoding branches and an attention-guided fusion head, the proposed model robustly anticipates pedestrian crossing intentions several frames before they occur. Extensive evaluations on the PIE and JAAD benchmarks demonstrate that MTF-Net surpasses recent transformer- and graph-based models, achieving up to 0.95 AUC on PIE and 0.94 AUC on JAAD, while maintaining real-time performance. The results highlight that reliable pedestrian intention prediction arises from principled multi-modal fusion rather than excessive architectural complexity.

AI.tldr: MTF-Net is a Multi-Modal Temporal Feature Fusion Network that predicts pedestrian crossing intentions by jointly modeling kinematic, appearance, and contextual cues using four modalities and GLU-based fusion modules.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for pedestrian intention prediction either model temporal dependencies within individual modalities or fuse modalities only at coarse semantic levels, limiting their effectiveness for safe autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interaction.
AI.method: MTF-Net integrates four complementary modalities (bounding-box dynamics, human pose keypoints, local context, and scene-level semantics) within a recurrent fusion framework enhanced by gated linear units (GLUs). The model uses three dedicated temporal encoding branches and an attention-guided fusion head to adaptively regulate cross-modal information flow across temporal scales.
AI.result: MTF-Net achieves up to 0.95 AUC on the PIE benchmark and 0.94 AUC on the JAAD benchmark, surpassing recent transformer- and graph-based models while maintaining real-time performance.
AI.conclusion: Reliable pedestrian intention prediction arises from principled multi-modal fusion rather than excessive architectural complexity, demonstrating that thoughtful fusion of complementary modalities can achieve state-of-the-art results with practical real-time capabilities.

authors: Henrique Curi de Miranda e Lourenço Alves Pereira
title: A Proposal for an Agentic AI Architecture to Support Multi-Domain Decision-Making in the Brazilian Armed Forces
comment: This paper was accepted for publication in the XXVIII SIGE (Simpósio de Aplicações Operacionais em Áreas de Defesa)
summary: The growing complexity of multi-domain operational environments (land, aerospace, naval, cyber, and electromagnetic spectrum) has increased the volume and velocity of data reaching command-and-control (C2) centers, straining the observe-orient-decide-act (OODA) decision cycle. Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems currently employed in defense are, in general, reactive and isolated tools that still rely heavily on human operators to integrate information, assess scenarios, and formulate courses of action. This paper proposes a conceptual Agentic AI architecture for AI systems that can plan, access data sources, execute tools, and act autonomously and audibly, aimed at supporting decision-making across the three Brazilian Armed Forces (Navy, Army, and Air Force). Four application fronts are discussed (decision support, situational analysis, feasibility studies, and countermeasure suggestion), as well as the data and sensor access requirements and the security and permission safeguards necessary for responsible employment across administrative, strategic, operational, and tactical contexts.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a conceptual Agentic AI architecture for defense command-and-control systems to address information overload in multi-domain operations. The architecture enables autonomous planning, data access, tool execution, and auditable actions across Brazil's three military branches.
AI.motivation: The increasing complexity of multi-domain operational environments (land, aerospace, naval, cyber, electromagnetic spectrum) has overwhelmed traditional OODA decision cycles with excessive data volume and velocity. Current AI systems in defense are reactive, isolated tools that still require heavy human involvement for information integration and decision-making.
AI.method: The paper proposes a conceptual Agentic AI architecture with four key capabilities: (1) planning, (2) data source access, (3) tool execution, and (4) autonomous and auditable action. Four application fronts are defined: decision support, situational analysis, feasibility studies, and countermeasure suggestion. The architecture includes requirements for data/sensor access and security/permission safeguards across administrative, strategic, operational, and tactical contexts.
AI.result: A proposed Agentic AI architecture framework designed to support decision-making across the Brazilian Armed Forces (Navy, Army, Air Force) in multi-domain environments, with defined application fronts and security requirements.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Agentic AI architecture aims to transform AI from a reactive tool to an active decision-support system capable of autonomous planning and action across military domains, while maintaining auditability and security safeguards necessary for responsible deployment.

title: Small Enough to Know Everything: The Fully-Enumerable Transformer as an Instrument for the Science of Delayed Generalization
comment: 9 pages, 2 figures. Code and per-seed run records will be released publicly
summary: Tiny transformers trained on fully-enumerable tasks occupy an unusual position in the study of grokking: every input can be evaluated, every generalization ceiling can be computed exactly, and hundreds of seeds cost minutes. We argue this regime is a scientific instrument with four capabilities that approximate settings cannot offer: (a) exact, falsifiable generalization ceilings; (b) task surgery that manipulates one structural variable while provably fixing all others; (c) direct observation of every weight; and (d) survival-time statistics over many seeds that recast "does not grok" as a censored observation. The obvious objection is that laws characterized at 10^4 parameters may not mean anything beyond them. We answer it with a preregistered conservation study: three task-side laws established at 12K parameters -- a recoverability-ceiling law, a role-conflict delay law, and a weight-decay response law -- are re-measured under an identical from-scratch protocol at 12K, 1M, and 50M parameters (a 4,000x span; 360 runs plus a 44-run control arm). The ceiling law and the delay law are conserved (0/144 Holm-corrected ceiling violations; Spearman rho >= 0.75 at every scale, permutation p < 1e-4), while the weight-decay law deforms systematically, steepening with scale. Preregistered controls show the 50M role-conflict deficit survives learning-rate adjustment and a tripled budget. Conservation was tested against criteria frozen before data collection, and one law's deformation shows the test could have failed. These results license the fully-enumerable transformer as a model organism for the task-side laws of delayed generalization: what it measures exactly, larger models largely obey -- and where they deviate, the deviation is itself lawful and measurable.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that tiny transformers trained on fully-enumerable tasks serve as a "scientific instrument" for studying grokking, offering exact generalization ceilings, task surgery capabilities, direct weight observation, and survival-time statistics. A preregistered conservation study tests three task-side laws (ceiling law, delay law, weight-decay law) across 4,000x parameter span (12K to 50M). Two laws are conserved while one deforms systematically, suggesting the small-scale model captures lawful generalizations that largely hold at larger scales.
AI.motivation: Address the objection that findings from small models (~10^4 parameters) may not generalize to larger models. The authors use a "model organism" approach: establish laws at small scale, then test if they hold at larger scales. This tests whether tiny transformers can serve as valid scientific instruments for understanding grokking phenomena.
AI.method: Preregistered conservation study with 360 runs plus 44-run control arm. Three task-side laws established at 12K parameters were re-measured at 12K, 1M, and 50M parameters (4,000x span). The study tested: (1) recoverability-ceiling law, (2) role-conflict delay law, (3) weight-decay response law. Controls included learning-rate adjustment and tripled budget at 50M scale.
AI.result: The ceiling law and delay law are conserved: 0/144 Holm-corrected ceiling violations; Spearman rho >= 0.75 at every scale with permutation p < 1e-4. The weight-decay law deforms systematically, steepening with scale. The 50M role-conflict deficit survives learning-rate adjustment and tripled budget controls.
AI.conclusion: The fully-enumerable transformer is a valid model organism for studying task-side laws of delayed generalization: what it measures exactly, larger models largely obey -- and where they deviate, the deviation is itself lawful and measurable. This validates small-scale studies as scientifically useful for understanding grokking.

title: MoSSGate: Memory-Modulated State-Space Gating for Skin Lesion Segmentation
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, accepted on International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing
summary: Accurate skin lesion segmentation is crucial for reliable computer-aided dermatological diagnosis, yet existing convolutional and transformer-based models often struggle to jointly capture long-range spatial dependencies and fine boundary details under limited computational budgets. This trade-off between global context modeling and boundary-aware localization frequently leads to over-segmentation, fragmented predictions, or missing thin peripheral structures. To address this challenge, we propose MoSSGate, a plug-and-play module for U-Net that integrates (i) boundary-aware spatial gating to restrict long-range propagation to informative regions, (ii) an external memory modulator that provides sample-adaptive dynamic control, and (iii) parallel 2D state-space modeling for efficient global context aggregation with linear complexity. The proposed design enables adaptive, context-aware information propagation while preserving sharp and accurate lesion boundaries. Extensive experiments on the ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018 benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy with strong efficiency, achieving 86.3% and 85.9% mIoU and 92.6% and 90.6% Dice, respectively, while requiring substantially fewer FLOPs than most competing CNN-based methods. These results highlight a favorable accuracy efficiency trade-off for high-resolution medical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: MoSSGate is a plug-and-play module for U-Net that enhances skin lesion segmentation by combining boundary-aware spatial gating, external memory modulation, and parallel 2D state-space modeling to jointly capture global context and fine boundary details with high efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing CNN and transformer-based models struggle to balance long-range spatial dependency capture and fine boundary detail preservation under limited computational budgets, leading to over-segmentation, fragmented predictions, or missing thin peripheral structures in skin lesion segmentation.
AI.method: The proposed MoSSGate module integrates three components: (i) boundary-aware spatial gating to restrict long-range propagation to informative regions, (ii) an external memory modulator for sample-adaptive dynamic control, and (iii) parallel 2D state-space modeling for efficient global context aggregation with linear complexity.
AI.result: On ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018 benchmarks, MoSSGate achieves 86.3% and 85.9% mIoU, and 92.6% and 90.6% Dice respectively, while requiring substantially fewer FLOPs than competing CNN-based methods, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
AI.conclusion: MoSSGate provides a promising solution for high-resolution medical image segmentation by achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with strong efficiency, effectively balancing global context modeling with boundary-aware localization.

title: UnifiedPlayers: Enhance Tool-Integrated Reasoning in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Self-evolving methods reduce the need for human-annotated trajectories by allowing tool-using agents to generate their own training data. Yet existing methods typically separate trajectory generation from evaluation, relying on static verifiers that cannot adapt to emerging failure modes or self-consistency signals that may reinforce errors shared across trajectories. Jointly adapting planning, execution, and evaluation offers a promising alternative, but introduces a fundamental coordination challenge: each component continuously changes the data or feedback used to train the others. We address this challenge with \textbf{UnifiedPlayers}, a cooperative framework comprising a Planning Player that generates tasks, an Execution Player that produces multi-turn trajectories with Python tool calls, and an Evaluation Player that constructs executable verifiers. We design role-specific rewards that coordinate the three players toward a shared learning objective under GRPO. Across two model backbones and twelve reasoning benchmarks, UnifiedPlayers outperforms the strongest prior baseline by at least 3.5\% on mathematical reasoning and 3.9\% on general reasoning tasks. Moreover, the learned verifier achieves 84.2\% adversarial detection accuracy, while its reward signal exhibits 2.03$\times$ higher per-question variance than a self-consistency baseline, providing more discriminative verifications. These results highlight cooperation among specialized players as a promising path toward self-enhanced tool-integrated agents.

AI.tldr: UnifiedPlayers is a cooperative framework with three specialized players (Planning, Execution, Evaluation) that jointly adapt to generate tasks, produce trajectories with tool calls, and construct executable verifiers for training tool-using agents, outperforming baselines by 3.5-3.9% across reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing self-evolving methods for tool-using agents separate trajectory generation from evaluation, relying on static verifiers that cannot adapt to emerging failure modes. This separation creates a coordination challenge where each component continuously changes the data or feedback used to train the others.
AI.method: UnifiedPlayers employs three role-specific players coordinated under GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization): Planning Player generates tasks, Execution Player produces multi-turn trajectories with Python tool calls, and Evaluation Player constructs executable verifiers. Role-specific rewards align the three players toward a shared learning objective.
AI.result: Across two model backbones and twelve reasoning benchmarks, UnifiedPlayers outperforms the strongest prior baseline by at least 3.5% on mathematical reasoning and 3.9% on general reasoning tasks. The learned verifier achieves 84.2% adversarial detection accuracy, with 2.03× higher per-question variance than self-consistency baseline.
AI.conclusion: Cooperation among specialized players offers a promising path toward self-enhanced tool-integrated agents. The framework successfully addresses the fundamental coordination challenge in jointly adapting planning, execution, and evaluation.

title: Support Thresholds, Not Algorithms, Limit Rare-Association Recovery in Co-Purchase Networks
summary: The support threshold of the Apriori algorithm involves a trade-off in conducting market basket analysis: the associations that occur frequently are noted with high threshold; however, the low ones lead to generating the large amount of rules. The paper compares five methods for co-purchase edge filtration on two grocery datasets: i.e., Instacart (3.2 million baskets) and Dunnhumby (208 thousand baskets), including Apriori, Apriori + lift post-filtering, top-$K$ ranking based on lift, and two methods based on networks, noise-corrected (NC) and disparity filter (DF). The top-$K$ method ensures the maximum average lift, while the NC achieves similar lift level by means of a single value of the significance parameter ($α$). These two methods recover substantially more rare high-lift associations than Apriori (80-100% against 22-28%). NC and top-$K$ select meaningfully different edges (18-29% non-overlapping): NC retains statistically validated pairs, while top-$K$ retains rare pairs with high lift but low statistical significance. A rolling-origin holdout evaluation shows that top-$K$ edges recur at higher rates at every split, but NC edges are ~12 pp more likely to remain statistically significant in the held-out network.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the trade-off problem in market basket analysis where high support thresholds miss rare but interesting associations, while low thresholds generate excessive rules. The authors compare five methods for co-purchase edge filtration on two large grocery datasets (Instacart and Dunnhumby), finding that network-based methods (noise-corrected) and top-K ranking outperform traditional Apriori in recovering rare high-lift associations, with different trade-offs between recurrence rates and statistical significance.
AI.motivation: The Apriori algorithm's support threshold creates a fundamental trade-off: high thresholds capture only frequent associations while missing rare ones; low thresholds generate an unwieldy number of rules. The authors aim to find methods that can recover rare high-lift associations without sacrificing statistical validity or generating excessive rules.
AI.method: The study compares five co-purchase edge filtration methods: (1) Apriori with standard support threshold, (2) Apriori with lift post-filtering, (3) top-K ranking based on lift, (4) noise-corrected (NC) network method, and (5) disparity filter (DF) network method. Evaluation is conducted on two grocery datasets: Instacart (3.2 million baskets) and Dunnhumby (208 thousand baskets). Methods are assessed on lift values, rare association recovery rates, edge overlap, and rolling-origin holdout performance.
AI.result: Top-K achieves maximum average lift, while NC achieves comparable lift using a single significance parameter (α). Both methods recover substantially more rare high-lift associations than Apriori (80-100% vs 22-28%). NC and top-K select meaningfully different edges (18-29% non-overlapping): NC retains statistically validated pairs while top-K retains rare pairs with high lift but low statistical significance. In holdout evaluation, top-K edges recur at higher rates across all splits, but NC edges are approximately 12 percentage points more likely to remain statistically significant in held-out networks.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that network-based methods (particularly noise-corrected) and top-K ranking offer practical alternatives to traditional Apriori for market basket analysis. Top-K is superior for identifying recurring purchasing patterns, while NC is better for finding statistically robust associations. The choice between methods depends on whether the goal is pattern recurrence or statistical reliability. The authors recommend the noise-corrected approach for applications requiring statistical validity.

title: A Two-Stage Multi-Scale Attention-Based Network for Weakly Supervised Cataract Fundus Image Enhancement
summary: Cataract is a major cause of vision loss and hinders further diagnosis. However, cataract fundus image enhancement often grapples with challenges such as limited paired cataract retinal images and insufficient recovery of fine details in the retinal images. To mitigate these challenges, we in this paper propose a two-stage multi-scale attention-based network (TSMSA-Net) for weakly supervised cataract fundus image enhancement. Our TSMSA-Net leverages the domain transformation to synthesis paired real-like cataract images, solving the problem of difficult acquisition of paired images. To further extract detailed information from fundus images and reduce the generation of artifacts during the enhancement process, we propose a multi-scale attention-based stage to learn more useful features for cataract image enhancement. Experimental results on Kaggle and ODIR-5K demonstrate that our TSMSA-Net outperforms current state-of-the-art cataract fundus images enhancement even without paired images and exhibits certain generalization ability. Experimental results on Kaggle and ODIR-5K datasets indicate that our TSMSA-Net outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods for cataract fundus image enhancement, even in the absence of paired images. Additionally, it demonstrates a certain level of generalization capability. The enhancement also can improve the performance of vessel segmentation and classification in cataract images.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes TSMSA-Net, a two-stage multi-scale attention-based network for weakly supervised cataract fundus image enhancement. It addresses the lack of paired cataract retinal images by using domain transformation to synthesize paired images, and employs multi-scale attention to extract fine details while reducing artifacts. The method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on Kaggle and ODIR-5K datasets and can improve vessel segmentation and classification tasks.
AI.motivation: Cataract is a major cause of vision loss that hinders further diagnosis. Current cataract fundus image enhancement faces two key challenges: (1) limited paired cataract retinal images for training, and (2) insufficient recovery of fine details in enhanced retinal images.
AI.method: The proposed TSMSA-Net consists of two stages: (1) A domain transformation module that synthesizes paired real-like cataract images to solve the paired image acquisition problem, and (2) A multi-scale attention-based stage that extracts detailed information from fundus images while reducing artifact generation during enhancement.
AI.result: Experimental results on Kaggle and ODIR-5K datasets demonstrate that TSMSA-Net outperforms current state-of-the-art cataract fundus image enhancement methods, even without paired images. The method also exhibits certain generalization ability and can improve performance of vessel segmentation and classification in cataract images.
AI.conclusion: The two-stage multi-scale attention-based network (TSMSA-Net) effectively addresses the challenges of limited paired training data and detail preservation in cataract fundus image enhancement. It achieves superior performance over existing methods and shows potential for improving downstream tasks like vessel segmentation and classification.

title: Solving Minimum Span Antibandwidth and Cyclic Antibandwidth Labeling Problems
summary: The Antibandwidth and Cyclic Antibandwidth problems are NP-hard graph labeling problems that aim to maximize the minimum (cyclic) distance between labels assigned to adjacent vertices. Extensive research on these problems has resulted in a variety of mathematical formulations and computational approaches. However, their minimum span perspective, in which a prescribed minimum (cyclic) distance is fixed and the objective is to minimize the label span, has received comparatively little attention. In this paper, we consider this complementary perspective by introducing the Minimum Span Antibandwidth/Cyclic Antibandwidth Labeling (MSABL/MSCABL) problems and developing a unified Boolean Satisfiability (SAT)-based framework for solving them. The SAT-based framework formulates MSABL/MSCABL as a sequence of decision problems and exploits their monotonicity to accelerate the search process. We also consider two SAT solving strategies, parallel and incremental SAT solving: the former examines multiple candidate spans concurrently, while the latter reuses a single SAT instance while progressively restricting the label domain. The proposed approaches are evaluated on benchmark instances from the Harwell-Boeing Sparse Matrix Collection and compared with CPLEXCP, CPLEXMIP, and Gurobi. The results show that SAT-based approaches are highly competitive in solution quality, with the parallel approach performing best overall for MSCABL and the incremental approach for MSABL. With the no-hole constraint, they remain competitive with CPLEXCP and significantly outperform CPLEXMIP and Gurobi, particularly for MSCABL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SAT solving as an exact approach for MSABL and MSCABL.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Minimum Span Antibandwidth/Cyclic Antibandwidth Labeling (MSABL/MSCABL) problems, which minimize label span given a fixed minimum distance constraint. A unified SAT-based framework with parallel and incremental solving strategies is developed. Results show SAT-based approaches are highly competitive, outperforming CPLEX and Gurobi solvers, particularly for MSCABL with the no-hole constraint.
AI.motivation: The Antibandwidth and Cyclic Antibandwidth problems have been extensively studied from a maximum minimum distance perspective, but the complementary minimum span perspective (fixing minimum distance and minimizing label span) has received comparatively little attention.
AI.method: The paper introduces MSABL/MSCABL problems and develops a unified SAT-based framework that formulates them as a sequence of decision problems, exploiting monotonicity to accelerate search. Two SAT solving strategies are compared: parallel SAT solving (examines multiple candidate spans concurrently) and incremental SAT solving (reuses a single SAT instance while progressively restricting the label domain).
AI.result: SAT-based approaches are highly competitive in solution quality. The parallel approach performs best overall for MSCABL, while the incremental approach performs best for MSABL. With the no-hole constraint, they remain competitive with CPLEXCP and significantly outperform CPLEXMIP and Gurobi, particularly for MSCABL.
AI.conclusion: SAT solving is an effective exact approach for MSABL and MSCABL problems, demonstrating superior performance over commercial solvers like CPLEX and Gurobi in many cases.

title: Robust Federated Q-Learning with Almost No Communication
comment: Accepted at the 2026 American Control Conference (ACC 2026)
summary: We consider a federated reinforcement learning setting involving $M$ agents, all of whom interact with a common Markov Decision Process (MDP). The agents exchange information via a central server to learn the optimal value function. Our goal is to understand to what extent one can hope for collaborative sample-complexity speedups in such a setting, when a small fraction of the agents are adversarial and can act arbitrarily. To that end, we propose Robust Fed-Q}, a federated Q-learning algorithm that blends ideas from both model-based and model-free RL, along with the median-of-means device from robust statistics. We prove that despite corruption, with high-probability, Robust Fed-Q (i) guarantees exact convergence to the optimal value function in the limit of infinite samples, and (ii) enjoys near-optimal finite-time rates that benefit from collaboration. In addition, our approach requires just $\tilde{O}(1)$ rounds of communication to achieve each of the above guarantees, a feature of independent interest in FL where communication is the major bottleneck.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses federated reinforcement learning where M agents collaborate to learn the optimal value function via a central server, with a focus on robustness against adversarial agents who can act arbitrarily. The proposed Robust Fed-Q algorithm combines model-based and model-free RL with robust statistics (median-of-means) to achieve convergence despite corruption.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand the extent of collaborative sample-complexity speedups in federated RL when a small fraction of agents are adversarial and can act arbitrarily. This is a practical concern in real-world federated learning where some participants may be compromised or malicious.
AI.method: The method proposes Robust Fed-Q, a federated Q-learning algorithm that blends ideas from both model-based and model-free RL, along with the median-of-means device from robust statistics. This combination allows the algorithm to handle adversarial/corrupted agents while still benefiting from collaborative learning.
AI.result: The paper proves that despite corruption, with high probability, Robust Fed-Q (i) guarantees exact convergence to the optimal value function in the limit of infinite samples, and (ii) enjoys near-optimal finite-time rates that benefit from collaboration. Additionally, the approach requires just O(1) rounds of communication to achieve each of the above guarantees.
